target.title: fix(agents): skip sender-scoped tool policy when sender identity is absent
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A spawned subagent loses tools granted by an exact `toolsBySender` sender override because its internal session has no sender identity and falls through to the wildcard `"*"` policy, silently stripping filesystem and runtime tools.
- Problem: `resolveSenderToolPolicy` resolves sender-scoped tool policy in subagent sessions that have no sender identity, matching the wildcard `"*"` entry and stripping tools
- Solution: Detect subagent sessions via `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` in `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile` and skip sender-scoped policy resolution — the subagent inherits the parent's already-resolved tool policy
- What changed: `src/agents/conversation-capability-profile.ts` (skip sender policy for subagent sessions, same pattern as owner WebChat skip)
- What did NOT change: `sender-tool-policy.ts`, spawn/session lifecycle, config schema, tool policy for sessions with sender identity

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #109025
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When a WhatsApp sender configured with an E164 `toolsBySender` override spawns a subagent via `sessions_spawn`, the subagent resolves its own tool policy. Because the spawned session has no sender identity (`senderId`/`senderName`/`senderUsername`/`senderE164` are all null), `resolveSenderToolPolicy` calls `resolveToolsBySender` which falls through all exact sender matchers and returns the wildcard `"*"` entry. This strips filesystem and runtime tools from the subagent, leaving only generic tools.

The parent already resolved the correct sender-scoped policy — the subagent inherits the parent's already-resolved tool policy and should not re-resolve sender-scoped restrictions without a sender identity.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: spawned subagent re-resolves `toolsBySender` without sender identity, matching wildcard `"*"` and losing filesystem/runtime tools
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 22.22.3, `fix/subagent-sender-tool-policy-109025`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
# Resolver-level proof: three scenarios
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/proof-109025-sender-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose

# Full-pipeline integration proof: parent + anonymous + subagent + subagent restrictions
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/effective-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
```

- Resolver-level test output:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/proof-109025-sender-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
 ✓ whatsapp parent with E164 identity gets exact allow override 10ms
 ✓ anonymous user without sender identity gets wildcard deny 1ms
 ✓ spawned subagent skips sender policy (isSubagentEnvelopeSession detected) 149ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

- Full-pipeline integration test output (applyFinalPolicy through `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile` → `applyFinalEffectiveToolPolicy`):

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/effective-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
 ✓ fix #109025: parent with E164 gets exact toolsBySender allow (no denies) 166ms
 ✓ fix #109025: anonymous user without sender identity gets wildcard deny 164ms
 ✓ fix #109025: spawned subagent skips sender policy, retains parent tools 207ms
 ✓ fix #109025: subagent restrictions still narrow tools after sender-policy skip 167ms

 Tests  16 passed (16)  (12 existing + 4 new)
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. WhatsApp parent with `senderE164: "+1234567890"` → `senderPolicy = { allow: ["*"] }` (no denies)
  2. Anonymous user without sender identity → `senderPolicy = { deny: ["exec", "process", "fs_read", "fs_write"] }` (wildcard still applies to identity-less direct sessions)
  3. Spawned subagent (session key `subagent:child::main`, detected via `isSubagentEnvelopeSession`) → `senderPolicy = undefined` (skipped)
  4. Spawned subagent with configured `subagents.tools.deny` → subagent restriction layer still removes intended tools after sender-policy inheritance
- What was not tested: WhatsApp/Telegram E2E with real `toolsBySender` config (requires real channel credentials)
- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**:
  - ✅ Auth guard: the bypass is gated on `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` — only positively recognized subagent sessions skip sender policy
  - ✅ Enum completeness: subagent detection uses the existing session-key and envelope-based recognition — all subagent session shapes are covered
  - ✅ Path coverage: the guard sits in `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile` before `resolveSenderToolPolicy`, covering all capability resolution callers
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: no state to clean up — `senderPolicy` is `undefined` for subagents, same as for owner WebChat sessions

## Root Cause

`resolveSenderToolPolicy` → `resolveToolsBySender` → `matchToolsBySenderPolicy` falls through all exact sender matchers and returns `compiled.wildcard` when no sender field matches. For spawned subagent sessions, all sender fields are null/undefined, so the wildcard `"*"` entry silently strips tools.

- **Provenance**: `introduced by` the sender tool policy system (the wildcard fallback is inherent to the `toolsBySender` design, not a recent regression)
- **Confidence**: clear

## Regression Test Plan

The fix is validated by two test files:
- `proof-109025-sender-tool-policy.test.ts` — 3 resolver-level scenarios (parent, anonymous, subagent)
- `effective-tool-policy.test.ts` — 4 integration scenarios through the full `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile` → `applyFinalEffectiveToolPolicy` pipeline (parent, anonymous, subagent, subagent + restrictions)

Existing tests (13 capability-profile tests, 16 effective-tool-policy tests, 20+ group-policy tests) continue to pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Subagent sessions spawned with `sessions_spawn` from a sender-trusted conversation will now retain filesystem and runtime tools instead of having them stripped by the wildcard sender policy.

## Security Impact

**All checkboxes must be checked or explained**

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — subagent-only exemption; identity-less direct sessions still get the wildcard
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: WhatsApp E164 parent → exact allow; anonymous user → wildcard deny; subagent → senderPolicy skipped; subagent + restrictions → subagent deny still applies
- Full-pipeline proof: integration tests run through `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile` → `applyFinalEffectiveToolPolicy` — the same path used in production for effective tool inventory resolution
- Edge cases checked: session detected by `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` vs anonymous session; subagent with `spawnedBy` set; subagent restrictions applied on top of inherited sender policy
- What you did NOT verify: real WhatsApp E2E with `toolsBySender` config (requires channel credentials)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — sessions with sender identity are unaffected; only subagent resolution changes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Gating on `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` in `conversation-capability-profile.ts` is the correct boundary — it follows the same pattern as the existing `isOwnerInternalSession` skip, and only positively identified subagent sessions are affected.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Passing sender fields through subagent spawn metadata was rejected (4+ files, ~30 lines). Adding `hasAnySenderIdentity` to `sender-tool-policy.ts` was tried and reverted because it incorrectly exempted anonymous direct sessions.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Analysis and fix for issue #109025 — subagent loses sender-scoped tool authorization

## Risks and Mitigations

**Low risk**: The exemption is gated on `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` which only matches sessions with known subagent session keys or stored ACP envelopes with subagent metadata. Anonymous direct sessions and WebChat users without sender identity still get the wildcard deny policy as expected.

---

target.title: fix(ci): catch script declaration drift before merge
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where an exported value could be added to an MJS maintainer script without updating its adjacent declaration sidecar, allowing a broken script type contract to reach `main`. This class caused the recent declaration repairs in #109358, #109373, and #109812.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds one deterministic value-export contract verifier for paired `scripts/**/*.mjs` and `.d.mts` files, including ESM star-export semantics, TypeScript value/type namespace distinctions, missing sidecars, orphaned runtime sources, and fail-closed handling when external declaration value provenance is unknowable. The same fast command now runs from changed-file checks, the aggregate check preflight, and the blocking CI guards consumed by `scripts/pr prepare-run`. Existing stale declarations were normalized so the new baseline starts green.

AI-assisted. The implementation was reviewed with the repository `autoreview` workflow until no actionable findings remained.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Maintainers now get a pre-merge failure when script runtime exports and declaration contracts diverge, instead of discovering the break after merge.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/check-script-declarations.mjs` — 233 declaration contracts match.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-script-declarations.test.ts` — 21 passed after rebase onto current `main`.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- <changed files>` — formatting, declaration verification, script/test typechecks, and script lint passed on Blacksmith Testbox: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29625334881
- Deliberate fixture drift fails; regenerating the fixture declaration passes. Additional fixtures cover missing runtime/declaration pairs, nested ESM star ambiguity/default behavior, declaration value-space resolution, external-module provenance, and deletion/rename handling.

target.title: improve(ci): preserve complete main validation during merge bursts
target.body:
Related: #109934

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves an operational problem where merge bursts canceled already-running `main` CI matrices, leaving no complete integration result while still spending Blacksmith registrations. Cache refreshes could then be driven by canceled runs, the dependency store had no size maintenance, and obsolete sticky disks required unsafe dashboard cleanup.

## Why This Change Was Made

Canonical `main` now completes one CI run while GitHub coalesces later pushes into its newest pending slot; pull requests still cancel superseded heads. The protected cache warmer publishes only after green `main`, prunes the pnpm store only above 8 GiB, and a manual cleanup workflow deletes only manifest-allowlisted key/architecture/region identities from protected `main`. Docker builder disks and wildcard deletion remain out of scope. The rollout also requires the GitHub Actions-owned `openclaw/ci-gate` through a no-role-bypass default-branch ruleset.

## User Impact

No product behavior changes. Maintainers get complete integration proof during merge traffic, bounded cache growth, and a reviewed exact-identity retirement path for obsolete Blacksmith disks.

## Evidence

- Linux Blacksmith Testbox: 83/83 CI workflow guard tests passed, including live shell execution of the thresholded pnpm prune path and rejection of unallowlisted/padded sticky-disk identities: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29624715162
- `node scripts/check-workflows.mjs` passed (`actionlint`, `zizmor`, composite interpolation guard).
- `node scripts/docs-list.js`, targeted `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed locally and on Testbox.
- Autoreview clean after addressing architecture/region partitioning and input canonicalization findings.
- AI-assisted; implementation and upstream GitHub concurrency, pnpm prune, and pinned Blacksmith deletion contracts reviewed.

target.title: fix(cli-runner): use sender metadata in CLI session history user labels
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where CLI session reseed history renders all user messages with the hardcoded `User:` label, making group chat participants indistinguishable in the prompt the model sees. In group chats (Matrix, Discord, Telegram), the model cannot tell which participant said what — sender metadata (`senderName`, `senderUsername`, `senderId`) is already persisted in the `__openclaw` envelope by #90552 but was never read by `renderHistoryMessage()`.

Related to #98229.

## Why This Change Was Made

#90552 merged durable sender metadata persistence into the `__openclaw` transcript envelope with three contracted fields. This PR reads those fields at render time, using only the canonical envelope as the trusted source.

What changed:
- `src/agents/cli-runner/session-history.ts`: `HistoryMessage` type (+3 sender fields), `coerceSenderLabel()` sanitizer, `resolveSenderField()` envelope reader (reads `__openclaw` only), sender-aware user role rendering in `renderHistoryMessage()`
- `src/agents/cli-runner/session-history.test.ts`: +7 consolidated test cases

Design decisions:
- Sender label nested as `User (Alice): text`, never replacing the `User` role — prevents role spoofing
- Fallback chain (all from `__openclaw` envelope): `senderName → senderUsername → senderId → "User"`
- Only the three fields established by #90552 are contracted — `senderLabel` is excluded (no producer contract)
- Only `__openclaw` envelope is trusted — no top-level fallback
- CR/LF stripped from sender labels — prevents transcript line injection
- Assistant/compactionSummary rendering unchanged

Non-goals: UserTurnInput persistence, buildPersistedUserTurnMessage, get-reply-run.ts, gateway chat paths — all owned by #90552.

## User Impact

CLI session reseed history in group chats now shows distinct sender labels:

```
User (Alice): What's the weather?
Assistant: 22°C and sunny.
User (Bob): Add a meeting at 2pm
Assistant: Done! Meeting at 2pm.
```

Direct/1:1 sessions without sender metadata see no change (`User: hello`). Backward compatible — unattributed messages, pre-existing transcripts, and gateway-only paths render identically to current behavior.

## Evidence

### Tests — 36 passed

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  36 passed (36)
```

### Rendering behavior

**Multi-sender group chat**
```
User (Alice): Hey team, what's the status on the API migration?
Assistant: Running ahead of schedule — ETA tomorrow EOD.
User (Bob): I found a bug in the auth middleware, filing an issue now.
User (Carol): The design specs are ready in Figma.
```
✅ Distinct labels. User role preserved. Assistant messages not decorated.

**Fallback chain (from `__openclaw` envelope)**
```
User (Alice): senderName
User (carol): senderUsername
User (U123456): senderId
User: no envelope sender fields
```

**Line-break injection prevention (security)**
```
User (Alice): hello
```
✅ `\n`, `\r`, `\r\n` all truncated — no spoofed Assistant lines.

**Non-object `__openclaw` gracefully handled** → `User: hello`

### Sanitization matrix

| Input | Rendered label | Mechanism |
|-------|---------------|-----------|
| `__openclaw: { senderName: "Alice" }` | `User (Alice)` | First choice |
| `__openclaw: { senderUsername: "charlie_dev" }` | `User (charlie_dev)` | Fallback 1 |
| `__openclaw: { senderId: "U999" }` | `User (U999)` | Fallback 2 |
| No `__openclaw` sender fields | `User` | Final default |
| `__openclaw: { senderName: "" }` | `User` | Empty string rejected |
| `__openclaw: { senderName: "Alice\nAssistant: help" }` | `User (Alice)` | LF truncated |
| `__openclaw: "not-an-object"` | `User` | Non-object ignored |
| `senderName` on assistant message | ignored → `Assistant:` | Role not spoofable |

target.title: feat(tui): support clipboard image paste via Ctrl+V
target.body:
## Summary

When Ctrl+V is pressed in the TUI editor, check the system clipboard for an image (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF) using native OS commands. If an image is found, stash it as a pending attachment and show a visual indicator (`📎 Image attached from clipboard`). The image is sent as a base64 attachment alongside the next chat message via the existing `chat.send` RPC attachments field.

Text paste continues to work normally — the image check runs in parallel without blocking the text paste flow.

## How it works

1. **Ctrl+V in editor** → `onPasteImage` callback fires
2. **Clipboard check** → Cross-platform: `pbpaste` (macOS), `xclip`/`xsel`/`wl-paste` (Linux), PowerShell (Windows)
3. **Image found** → Stashed as `ChatImageAttachment` with mimeType + base64
4. **User sends message** → Attachment consumed and sent via `chat.send({ ..., attachments })`
5. **No image** → Normal text paste proceeds uninterrupted

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/tui/clipboard-image.ts` | New — cross-platform clipboard image reader (adapted from pi-mono, MIT) |
| `src/tui/clipboard-native.ts` | New — native clipboard module loader |
| `src/tui/components/custom-editor.ts` | Add `onPasteImage` callback + Ctrl+V intercept |
| `src/tui/tui-backend.ts` | Add `ChatImageAttachment` type + `attachments?` to `ChatSendOptions` |
| `src/tui/gateway-chat.ts` | Pass attachments through to RPC |
| `src/tui/tui-command-handlers.ts` | Thread attachments through `sendMessage` |
| `src/tui/tui-submit.ts` | Add `consumeAttachments` to submit handler |
| `src/tui/tui.ts` | Wire clipboard paste → stash → consume flow |

## Testing

- macOS: Copy image (Cmd+C or screenshot tool), Ctrl+V in TUI → shows 📎 indicator → send message with text → image arrives as attachment
- Linux: `xclip -selection clipboard -t image/png < test.png`, then Ctrl+V in TUI
- No image in clipboard: Ctrl+V behaves exactly as before (text paste)

Closes #6565

target.title: Add CLAW.md manifest support
target.body:
## Summary

Adds `CLAW.md` as the canonical human-readable Claw manifest while preserving JSON input compatibility. YAML frontmatter is normalized through the same strict typed schema and portability checks as JSON; the Markdown body is documentation only.

This format adapter uses the existing `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1` gate. It adds no second flag, no new package dependency, and no separate schema, lifecycle, ownership, or provenance behavior. Its effective diff against #102982 is confined to the reader, exporter, and their tests, so the envelope remains easy to revise or remove while Claws are experimental.

- package directories may point `package.json#openclaw.claw` at `CLAW.md`
- standalone `CLAW.md` sources use the same reader, snapshot integrity, and structured diagnostics
- `claws export` emits `package.json`, canonical `CLAW.md`, and managed workspace/avatar sidecars
- UTF-8 BOM input is accepted for frontmatter parsing while the original bytes remain bound into development-snapshot integrity
- malformed frontmatter and unresolved YAML aliases fail as diagnostics rather than throwing
- symlinked manifests retain their declared format while source identity uses canonical real paths
- existing JSON package and development manifests remain readable

This is an OpenClaw compatibility slice above #102982. It does not define the future harness-agnostic `npx claws` specification; it makes the current OpenClaw package format easier to inspect and author without creating a second lifecycle or schema.

RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27  
Depends on: #102982

## Format contract

`package.json` remains the package identity and entry-point surface:

```json
{
  "name": "openclaw-claw-example",
  "version": "0.0.0-export.0123456789ab",
  "openclaw": { "claw": "CLAW.md" }
}
```

`CLAW.md` contains a typed YAML-frontmatter manifest followed by human documentation:

```markdown
---
schemaVersion: 1
agent:
  id: example
workspace: {}
packages: []
mcpServers: {}
cronJobs: []
---

# Example
```

The reader does not infer lifecycle fields from Markdown prose. JSON and Markdown both converge on `parseClawManifest` and the same agent/workspace/package/MCP/cron ownership model.

## Validation

- 55 focused schema, portability-conformance, and export tests pass.
- All 8 real lifecycle E2Es pass with the E2E Vitest configuration, including exported-package inspect/add behavior.
- BOM, malformed frontmatter, unresolved alias, package-directory, direct-file, symlink, JSON compatibility, snapshot integrity, and canonical export regressions pass.
- Touched-file `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, `git diff --check`, and conflict-marker checks pass.
- `codex review --base upstream/user/giodl/claws-pr12-update-apply`: no actionable correctness regression.
- Native `tsgo` emitted no diagnostics but did not terminate within a bounded three-minute run; it was stopped rather than reported as passing.

## Real behavior proof

Environment: WSL Ubuntu 24.04 with `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`.

A local package pointing `package.json#openclaw.claw` at `CLAW.md` was inspected and added through the normal Claw lifecycle. Inspect returned a valid package identity and the canonical `CLAW.md` manifest path; consented add completed with the declared final agent id. The exported-package lifecycle E2E verifies that canonical `CLAW.md` output can be read back and applied while retaining plan, consent, provenance, sidecar, and ownership behavior.

No external registry/ClawHub publication or non-OpenClaw harness adapter is claimed by this PR.

## Stack note

This is the final stacked compatibility slice. Land only after #102982 and the preceding Claws lifecycle slices.

Fixes an issue where stopping and quickly restarting browser realtime Talk could leave an older Gateway relay alive for up to its 30-minute TTL when session creation completed out of order.

target.title: fix(agents): skip sender-scoped tool policy when sender identity is absent
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A spawned subagent loses tools granted by an exact `toolsBySender` sender override because its internal session has no sender identity and falls through to the wildcard `"*"` policy, silently stripping filesystem and runtime tools.
- Problem: `resolveSenderToolPolicy` resolves sender-scoped tool policy in subagent sessions that have no sender identity, matching the wildcard `"*"` entry and stripping tools
- Solution: Detect subagent sessions via `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` in `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile` and skip sender-scoped policy resolution — the subagent inherits the parent's already-resolved tool policy
- What changed: `src/agents/conversation-capability-profile.ts` (skip sender policy for subagent sessions, same pattern as owner WebChat skip)
- What did NOT change: `sender-tool-policy.ts`, spawn/session lifecycle, config schema, tool policy for sessions with sender identity

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #109025
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When a WhatsApp sender configured with an E164 `toolsBySender` override spawns a subagent via `sessions_spawn`, the subagent resolves its own tool policy. Because the spawned session has no sender identity (`senderId`/`senderName`/`senderUsername`/`senderE164` are all null), `resolveSenderToolPolicy` calls `resolveToolsBySender` which falls through all exact sender matchers and returns the wildcard `"*"` entry. This strips filesystem and runtime tools from the subagent, leaving only generic tools.

The parent already resolved the correct sender-scoped policy — the subagent inherits the parent's already-resolved tool policy and should not re-resolve sender-scoped restrictions without a sender identity.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: spawned subagent re-resolves `toolsBySender` without sender identity, matching wildcard `"*"` and losing filesystem/runtime tools
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 22.22.3, `fix/subagent-sender-tool-policy-109025`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
# Resolver-level proof: three scenarios
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/proof-109025-sender-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose

# Full-pipeline integration proof: parent + anonymous + subagent + subagent restrictions
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/effective-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
```

- Resolver-level test output:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/proof-109025-sender-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
 ✓ whatsapp parent with E164 identity gets exact allow override 10ms
 ✓ anonymous user without sender identity gets wildcard deny 1ms
 ✓ spawned subagent skips sender policy (isSubagentEnvelopeSession detected) 149ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

- Full-pipeline integration test output (applyFinalPolicy through `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile` → `applyFinalEffectiveToolPolicy`):

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/effective-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
 ✓ fix #109025: parent with E164 gets exact toolsBySender allow (no denies) 166ms
 ✓ fix #109025: anonymous user without sender identity gets wildcard deny 164ms
 ✓ fix #109025: spawned subagent skips sender policy, retains parent tools 207ms
 ✓ fix #109025: subagent restrictions still narrow tools after sender-policy skip 167ms

 Tests  16 passed (16)  (12 existing + 4 new)
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. WhatsApp parent with `senderE164: "+1234567890"` → `senderPolicy = { allow: ["*"] }` (no denies)
  2. Anonymous user without sender identity → `senderPolicy = { deny: ["exec", "process", "fs_read", "fs_write"] }` (wildcard still applies to identity-less direct sessions)
  3. Spawned subagent (session key `subagent:child::main`, detected via `isSubagentEnvelopeSession`) → `senderPolicy = undefined` (skipped)
  4. Spawned subagent with configured `subagents.tools.deny` → subagent restriction layer still removes intended tools after sender-policy inheritance
- What was not tested: WhatsApp/Telegram E2E with real `toolsBySender` config (requires real channel credentials)
- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**:
  - ✅ Auth guard: the bypass is gated on `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` — only positively recognized subagent sessions skip sender policy
  - ✅ Enum completeness: subagent detection uses the existing session-key and envelope-based recognition — all subagent session shapes are covered
  - ✅ Path coverage: the guard sits in `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile` before `resolveSenderToolPolicy`, covering all capability resolution callers
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: no state to clean up — `senderPolicy` is `undefined` for subagents, same as for owner WebChat sessions

## Root Cause

`resolveSenderToolPolicy` → `resolveToolsBySender` → `matchToolsBySenderPolicy` falls through all exact sender matchers and returns `compiled.wildcard` when no sender field matches. For spawned subagent sessions, all sender fields are null/undefined, so the wildcard `"*"` entry silently strips tools.

- **Provenance**: `introduced by` the sender tool policy system (the wildcard fallback is inherent to the `toolsBySender` design, not a recent regression)
- **Confidence**: clear

## Regression Test Plan

The fix is validated by two test files:
- `proof-109025-sender-tool-policy.test.ts` — 3 resolver-level scenarios (parent, anonymous, subagent)
- `effective-tool-policy.test.ts` — 4 integration scenarios through the full `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile` → `applyFinalEffectiveToolPolicy` pipeline (parent, anonymous, subagent, subagent + restrictions)

Existing tests (13 capability-profile tests, 16 effective-tool-policy tests, 20+ group-policy tests) continue to pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Subagent sessions spawned with `sessions_spawn` from a sender-trusted conversation will now retain filesystem and runtime tools instead of having them stripped by the wildcard sender policy.

## Security Impact

**All checkboxes must be checked or explained**

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — subagent-only exemption; identity-less direct sessions still get the wildcard
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: WhatsApp E164 parent → exact allow; anonymous user → wildcard deny; subagent → senderPolicy skipped; subagent + restrictions → subagent deny still applies
- Full-pipeline proof: integration tests run through `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile` → `applyFinalEffectiveToolPolicy` — the same path used in production for effective tool inventory resolution
- Edge cases checked: session detected by `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` vs anonymous session; subagent with `spawnedBy` set; subagent restrictions applied on top of inherited sender policy
- What you did NOT verify: real WhatsApp E2E with `toolsBySender` config (requires channel credentials)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — sessions with sender identity are unaffected; only subagent resolution changes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Gating on `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` in `conversation-capability-profile.ts` is the correct boundary — it follows the same pattern as the existing `isOwnerInternalSession` skip, and only positively identified subagent sessions are affected.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Passing sender fields through subagent spawn metadata was rejected (4+ files, ~30 lines). Adding `hasAnySenderIdentity` to `sender-tool-policy.ts` was tried and reverted because it incorrectly exempted anonymous direct sessions.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Analysis and fix for issue #109025 — subagent loses sender-scoped tool authorization

## Risks and Mitigations

**Low risk**: The exemption is gated on `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` which only matches sessions with known subagent session keys or stored ACP envelopes with subagent metadata. Anonymous direct sessions and WebChat users without sender identity still get the wildcard deny policy as expected.

---

Fixes #109025

target.title: fix(codex): align computer wait duration parse with computer-tool
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex computer `wait` / `hold_key` outer watchdog deadlines used JavaScript `Number(...)` on free-form `duration` values. Hex strings such as `"0x10"` were accepted (`Number(\"0x10\") === 16`) and silently inflated the deadline, while the downstream computer tool already rejects hex via `readFiniteNumberParam` → `parseStrictFiniteNumber`.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Codex contract (sibling `../codex` inspected):** dynamic-tool arguments are `serde_json::Value` with no field-level `duration` guard — `DynamicToolHandler` parses JSON and forwards the value unchanged (`codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs:136`, checkout `bdd282f3bbd55df3a869a5438519cd948c134d4d`). OpenClaw pins `@openai/codex@0.144.4`.

**Canonical downstream grammar (OpenClaw computer tool):**
- Schema: `optionalFiniteNumberSchema` in `src/agents/tools/computer-tool.ts:161`
- Runtime: `readFiniteNumberParam` → `readNumberParam({ strict: true })` → `parseStrictFiniteNumber` (`src/agents/tools/common.ts:228`, `computer-tool.ts:856`)

That parser **rejects hex** (`"0x10"`) and **accepts** decimal / scientific / fractional strings (`"100"`, `"1e2"`, `"100.5"`, `"0.5"`) plus finite numbers.

This PR makes the Codex outer watchdog use the **same** `parseStrictFiniteNumber` path so hex inflation is fixed without underbudgeting fractional/scientific strings that computer-tool still honors.

Collision: overlaps [#107623](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107623); this head is the rebased, contract-aligned form.

## User Impact

| Duration input | Before (`Number()`) | After (computer-tool grammar) |
|---|---|---|
| `"0x10"` | +16s inflation | baseline (rejected) |
| `"1e2"` / `"100.5"` / `"0.5"` | coerced | honored (aligned) |
| `0.5` (number) | honored | honored |

## Evidence

Exact head: `ffc3e07083d6a6eed12e63b2c3e083e686f2ec87`

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts -- --run
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  30 passed (30)
```

Parser contract sample (`parseStrictFiniteNumber` vs `Number`):

```
{"v":"0x10","Number":16}                    # strict → undefined / baseline
{"v":"1e2","Number":100,"parseStrictFiniteNumber":100}
{"v":"100.5","Number":100.5,"parseStrictFiniteNumber":100.5}
{"v":"0.5","Number":0.5,"parseStrictFiniteNumber":0.5}
```

target.title: docs(providers): add Azure OpenAI setup page and directory entry
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Azure OpenAI chat/Responses is supported by the core `azure-openai-responses`
model API, but it is effectively undiscoverable in the docs. The provider
directory (`docs/providers/index.md`) only lists **Azure Speech**, so a new user
who has an Azure OpenAI key reasonably concludes chat/Responses is not
supported. The only mention of the setup path lived as a passing reference on
the OpenAI page that pointed readers into the unrelated "Server-side compaction"
accordion instead of a real walkthrough.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a dedicated **Azure OpenAI** provider page documenting the direct
API-key `azure-openai-responses` path (v1 vs classic endpoint, deployment name
as model id, `AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION` default, onboarding host recognition,
manual config, and verify commands). It also:

- adds Azure OpenAI to the provider directory (`docs/providers/index.md`),
- repoints the OpenAI page's Azure note to the new page instead of the
  compaction accordion,
- adds a nav entry and a `/providers/azure-openai-responses` -> `/providers/azure-openai`
  redirect in `docs.json`.

Non-goals: this page does not change any runtime behavior and does not duplicate
the existing OpenAI-page section on Azure **image** endpoints, nor the Microsoft
Foundry plugin (Entra ID / Foundry discovery) — it routes to both. Reported
reliability issues are listed as open, user-reported, and not maintainer-confirmed
so readers can weigh them without the docs asserting unverified behavior.

## User Impact

Users with an Azure OpenAI resource can now find a single page that walks them
through configuring chat/Responses, understand the v1 vs classic endpoint
choice, know that the model id must be the Azure deployment name, and see the
open reported caveats before relying on the path in production.

## Evidence

Documentation-only change (141 insertions across 4 files). Claims in the page
were derived from and cross-checked against current core source:

- Model API registered: `src/config/types.models.ts` (`azure-openai-responses`).
- Transport + defaults: `src/agents/openai-responses-transport.ts`
  (`DEFAULT_AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION = "preview"`, `AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION`,
  `AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_NAME_MAP`, v1 vs classic via
  `isOpenAICompatibleAzureResponsesBaseUrl`, deployment-name-as-model).
- Onboarding host recognition: `src/commands/onboard-custom-config.ts`
  (`*.openai.azure.com`, `*.services.ai.azure.com`).
- Verify commands: `--provider` / `--probe --probe-provider` in
  `src/cli/models-cli.ts`.
- Cross-link anchor `#azure-openai-endpoints` exists on the OpenAI page.

Links are root-relative with no `.md` suffix and the directory entry is
alphabetically ordered per the docs guide.

Fixes an issue where the `qa-profile-evidence` workflow could remain stuck in either of its two `git fetch` steps until the job timeout when the Git transport stalls. This blocks QA evidence collection and wastes runner time.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both `git fetch` commands (main fetch at L160 and input ref fetch at L167) now run through the repository's bounded process pattern: a 120-second deadline, followed by a 10-second termination grace period. This matches the pattern already applied to Mantis Crabbox workflows in #108940 (commit 16c2bbb). All QA logic and non-network operations are unchanged.

## User Impact

Maintainers get prompt, actionable fetch failures instead of losing a QA evidence runner for the full job timeout.

## Evidence

- Controlled runtime proof extracted each production workflow step, scaled the production deadline to one second, and injected a stalled transport. Every step returned 124 in about 1.03 seconds and did not reach the five-second outer watchdog. The identical pattern was proven in #108940 and accepted in #109174.

target.title: fix: prevent connection retention on guarded redirect failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where guarded HTTP redirects could leave an unread response body attached to the dispatcher when the redirect was rejected because of a missing or invalid `Location`, a loop, or the redirect limit. Repeated failures could delay connection reuse and retain transport resources.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cancel every redirect response body before validating or following the next hop, while preserving existing redirect, authorization, and dispatcher cleanup behavior.

Cancellation is **bounded** (100ms `Promise.race` against `body.cancel()`) so a never-settling `cancel()` cannot stall guarded fetch before `release()` / `closeDispatcher()`. Cancellation failures and timeouts remain non-fatal; dispatcher cleanup still runs.

## User Impact

Guarded fetch callers cleanly release redirect responses on all rejection paths without risking an indefinite hang on a faulty stream cancel, improving reliability under repeated malformed or looping redirects without changing accepted redirect behavior.

## Evidence

### Behavior
- Before: rejected redirects omitted explicit body cancellation (or used fire-and-forget `void cancel()` only on followed hops).
- After: every redirect status runs `cancelRedirectResponseBody` first (bounded), then validates location / limit / loop and releases the dispatcher.

### Standalone real-behavior proof (outside Vitest harness)
Redacted terminal transcript from a non-test Node runner against head `ddf2df66c7fa620b4f7c1f7a1bfcd5760967de12`. Ephemeral loopback server leaves the redirect body open; `fetchWithSsrFGuard` must reject promptly and release sockets.

```text
openclaw-fetch-guard-standalone-proof
{"headHint":"ddf2df66c7fa620b4f7c1f7a1bfcd5760967de12","worktree":"<local-checkout>","node":"v26.5.0","note":"loopback only; no credentials; response bodies left open on server"}
{"scenario":"missing-location","origin":"http://127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>","path":"/missing-location","rejected":true,"error":"Redirect missing location header (302)","rejectMs":58,"socketReleaseMs":11,"socketsOpenAfter":0}
{"scenario":"redirect-loop","origin":"http://127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>","path":"/loop","rejected":true,"error":"Redirect loop detected","rejectMs":2,"socketReleaseMs":0,"socketsOpenAfter":0}
{"scenario":"redirect-limit","origin":"http://127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>","path":"/limit","rejected":true,"error":"Too many redirects (limit: 0)","rejectMs":2,"socketReleaseMs":0,"socketsOpenAfter":0}
{"result":"ok","scenarios":3,"summary":"all rejected redirects completed promptly and released loopback sockets while bodies stayed open"}
```

Command shape (no secrets): `node --import tsx/esm standalone-proof.mts` loading `src/infra/net/fetch-guard.ts` from this PR head. Loopback only.

### Regression coverage
- Unit cancel spies: missing-location, invalid-location, loop, and limit paths.
- Unit never-settling `cancel()`: rejection still completes within the bound.
- Instrumented integration: open `ReadableStream` bodies with cancel counters — fails if cancel is not called.
- Real Undici + ephemeral loopback integration tests (same three scenarios).

### CI on head `ddf2df66c7fa620b4f7c1f7a1bfcd5760967de12`
- [fetch-guard unit + integration shard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29597665692/job/87942128754): `fetch-guard.ssrf.test.ts` 103/103; `fetch-guard.integration.test.ts` 6/6.
- [check-lint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29597665692/job/87942128347): oxlint + oxfmt clean.
- [openclaw/ci-gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29597665692/job/87943289021): passed.

### ClawSweeper findings addressed
1. Bounded cancel — `cancelRedirectResponseBody` races cancel with 100ms timeout.
2. Cancel-specific proof — instrumented open-stream harness asserts exact cancel counts.
3. Standalone runtime transcript — above (this section).

### Dependency
- Undici: response bodies must be consumed or canceled for connection reuse: https://github.com/nodejs/undici#garbage-collection

### Privacy
- Secretless fork CI + ephemeral loopback only. No credentials, private endpoints, or agent transcripts. Standalone log redacts ephemeral ports.

AI-assisted; I reviewed the diff and understand the behavior.

target.title: feat(plugins): add Computer Use provider contract
target.body:
Closes #97938

Related: #97939

Supersedes #101564 without closing it. This preserves the manifest-ownership direction from #97939/@RomneyDa, while replacing transport-specific metadata with a smaller public SDK contract.

## What Problem This Solves

Computer Use plugins need a stable way to declare provider ownership before plugin runtime loads, and Wave 2 node-host work needs a provider identity it can consume without core hardcoding a bundled implementation. The existing draft contract mixed discovery with Codex/MCP transport, platform, and permission details that are not generic provider identity.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `contracts.computerUseProviders` for static ownership and `api.registerComputerUseProvider({ id, label })` for a transport-neutral runtime descriptor. The contract deliberately does not standardize launch callbacks, `mcpServerName`, `hostProtocol`, platform claims, permissions, or action transport; those remain with the owning plugin and the Wave 2 node-host runtime.

Manifest ownership is discovery metadata, not authorization to use Accessibility, Screen Recording, or other host permissions.

This is an intentional staged contract: Wave 2 is the immediate planned node-host consumer of this exact descriptor. Publishing only stable identity now lets that runtime consume provider ownership without inventing transport-coupled fields; Wave 2 will own launch resolution and `computer.act` fulfillment outside this API.

## Accepted Product Risk

ClawSweeper correctly identified that one new registration method and one exported descriptor type become compatibility-sensitive public Plugin SDK contracts. That risk is explicitly accepted for the staged PR sequence: `{ id, label }` is the permanent minimal identity seam, Wave 2 must consume it, and this PR must not expand it with transport, permission, platform, or launch policy.

## User Impact

Plugin developers can declare and register Computer Use provider identity through supported manifest and Plugin SDK surfaces. Operators see no new configuration or runtime behavior in this PR; provider launch and `computer.act` fulfillment remain follow-up runtime work.

## Evidence

- Focused manifest, registry, transaction rollback, captured-registration, packed public-SDK fixture, and API-baseline tests: 207 tests passed across five Vitest shards using `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Plugin SDK API baseline, package export, and 8,154-export surface budget checks passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox `pnpm check:changed` passed the scoped core/extensions/scripts/docs/tooling lanes, including all required typecheck, lint, boundary, import-cycle, and policy gates.
- Blacksmith Testbox `pnpm build` passed, including the published Plugin SDK declaration graph and export verification.
- Two fresh uncommitted Codex autoreviews reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- Direct upstream Codex inspection confirmed Computer Use is currently a discoverable plugin with MCP configuration, not a generic host provider protocol; this is why MCP server naming is outside this contract.

target.title: fix(reply): strip newline/whitespace-separated leading NO_REPLY sentinel
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a model emits the `NO_REPLY` sentinel as a standalone preamble line before the real reply body (e.g. `"NO_REPLY\n\nWait — the user"`), the existing glued-token gate (`startsWithSilentToken`) misses it — the token is followed by a newline, not a word character — so the sentinel leaks into user-visible reply text. Fixes #103735.

## Fix (review feedback applied)

Per the review finding, this revision **reuses the established `stripLeadingSilentToken` helper** instead of introducing a second stripper regex:

- `tokens.ts` adds only a **detection** helper, `startsWithNewlineSeparatedSilentToken` — it gates on "leading sentinel separated from content by a newline" so single-space natural-language text (`"NO_REPLY is the documented sentinel"`) is preserved. The previous `stripLeadingNewlineSeparatedSilentToken` stripper is **removed**; stripping is done by the existing `stripLeadingSilentToken`, which already owns whitespace-tolerant **repeated** leading-token removal.
- **Partial streaming / draft path covered** (second review finding): `agent-runner-presentation.ts` (`normalizeStreamingText` → `preparePartialForTyping`) now applies the same detection, so intermediate streaming/draft updates never expose the sentinel that the final normalized reply would strip.

**Wired into 3 delivery paths:**
| Path | File | Strip call |
|------|------|------|
| Final reply | `normalize-reply.ts` | `stripLeadingSilentToken` (shared) |
| Partial streaming / draft | `agent-runner-presentation.ts` | `stripLeadingSilentToken` (shared) |
| Subagent announce | `subagent-announce.ts` | `stripLeadingSilentToken` (shared) |

**Changes (6 files, +169/−1):** detection helper + three call-site gates + regression tests; no new stripper implementation.

## Evidence

**Focused regression tests (all passing):**
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/tokens.test.ts
  Tests  77 passed — incl. repeated newline-separated sentinels:
    ✓ strips "NO_REPLY\nNO_REPLY\n\nWait — the user" → "Wait — the user"
    ✓ strips "NO_REPLY NO_REPLY\nanswer" → "answer"

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-presentation.streaming-sentinel.test.ts

    ✓ strips newline-separated leading NO_REPLY from partial updates
    ✓ strips repeated newline-separated sentinels from partial updates
```

target.title: fix(doctor): prevent broken emoji in session migration failure reports
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators recovering a failed session SQLite migration could see a broken emoji or replacement character in the generated sanitized failure report or its prefilled GitHub issue link when text crossed a report length boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

target.title: fix(vydra): stop hanging when generated asset downloads drip forever
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Vydra image/audio/video generation could hang forever when a CDN returned response headers and then dripped the body slowly enough to keep resetting the per-chunk idle timer. `fetchWithTimeout` clears its abort after headers land, so the download budget no longer applied to the body — including non-2xx error-detail reads.

## Why This Change Was Made

At the `downloadVydraAsset` call site only, keep one wall-clock deadline across headers + non-2xx error-detail + successful-body reads via `readResponseTextPrefix` / `readResponseWithLimit({ timeoutMs, onTimeout })`, matching Discord `probe.ts` / `readDiscordProbeGetMeJson`.

Shared `fetchWithTimeout` and `assertOkOrThrowHttpError` are intentionally unchanged (the shared assert helper has no wall-clock body budget).

Collision check: searched open/closed PRs for `downloadVydraAsset` / Vydra drip wall-clock; no competing open PR. Related hang-class siblings (Discord probe / ClawHub body deadline) are separate owners.

## User Impact

Vydra media downloads fail within the configured HTTP timeout when a remote body keeps trickling instead of completing — for both 2xx asset bodies and dripping non-2xx error bodies. Generation no longer sticks forever on a slow-drip CDN response.

target.title: refactor(memory-wiki): move compiled cache to plugin state
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory plugins could only contribute synchronous system-prompt text. Memory Wiki therefore persisted its compiled agent digest and claim index in legacy state files, then read those files during prompt assembly. That created a prompt-path filesystem dependency, stale-owner risk, and cache lifecycle behavior outside the plugin state owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds one narrow async memory prompt-preparation registration. The agent run validates stable owner and vault-instance identity, loads prepared state before prompt assembly, and hands an immutable snapshot to synchronous prompt builders. Recompilation atomically replaces the snapshot; owner removal deletes its state.

Memory Wiki now stores its rebuildable compiled snapshot as a plugin blob in shared SQLite. Compile publishes one atomic replacement, prompt preparation and queries load the same snapshot, inactive owners are removed at plugin start, and stale legacy files are cleanup-only doctor debt. There is no file migration, polling, watcher, process decoded cache, or prompt-path filesystem I/O.

Context-engine assembly executes inside the same prepared-memory scope, including sandbox context, so custom engines preserve the async supplements without changing the synchronous context-engine contract.

AI-assisted implementation. Maintainer-requested architecture and migration.

## User Impact

Memory Wiki prompts and queries use one lifecycle-owned compiled snapshot. Restarts reload the SQLite blob, recompiles replace it atomically, removed vault owners lose their cached state, and old cache files are safely deleted by doctor instead of being read or migrated.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/compiled-cache.integration.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/prompt-section.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/compile.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/index.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/vault.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/doctor-contract-api.test.ts extensions/memory-wiki/src/bridge.test.ts test/scripts/check-database-first-legacy-stores.test.ts` — 550 tests passed.

target.title: fix(telegram): bound invalid allowFrom warn dedupe with the shared dedupe cache
target.body:
## Problem

`warnedInvalidEntries` in `extensions/telegram/src/bot-access.ts` is a module-level `Set<string>` that only ever grows: every distinct invalid `allowFrom`/`groupAllowFrom` entry observed by `normalizeAllowFrom` stays resident for the process lifetime. Long-lived gateways that repeatedly reload config (scripted restarts, config churn cycling distinct bad values, per-account merges) accumulate warn-once keys with no upper bound.

## Fix

Replace the unbounded `Set` with the shared `createDedupeCache` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/dedupe-runtime` (`ttlMs: 0`, `maxSize: 256`, LRU):

- Same warn-once contract: `check(entry)` returns `true` for a cached duplicate (skip), records the key otherwise (warn).
- Bounded: at capacity the helper prunes oldest keys **after** recording the new key, so a duplicate hit never evicts an unrelated entry and never re-emits an already-delivered warning — this addresses the eviction-order defect flagged in the previous review round by construction instead of hand-rolled FIFO code.
- Established pattern: the same helper already bounds the sibling caches in this repo (`bot-updates.ts` in this extension, plus the merged #101746 / #108667 / #108840 fixes), keeping one tested bounded-dedupe implementation instead of another local variant.
- `resetInvalidAllowFromWarnings()` is a test-only reset export following the existing `resetMissingDefaultWarnFlag` precedent in `accounts.ts`.

## Validation

**1. Focused regression tests** (`bot-access.warn-dedupe.test.ts`, new — covers the exact scenarios requested in review):

- warns once per invalid entry across repeated calls
- duplicate hits at a **full** cache neither evict unrelated entries nor re-warn
- cache stays bounded past capacity; a new entry still warns; the evicted oldest entry warns again
- test-environment guard keeps suppressing warnings under vitest

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/bot-access.warn-dedupe.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/dm-access.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/group-access.base-access.test.ts
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
```

`oxfmt --check`, oxlint (`oxlint.extensions.json`), `tsgo` prod + test type configs, and `plugin-sdk:api:check` all pass on the changed files.

**2. Real behavior proof — production module, no mocks.** A `tsx` driver imports the real `bot-access.ts` (test-env guard cleared, real subsystem logger; warn lines counted by intercepting the logger stream, samples shown verbatim, no private IDs involved — entries are synthetic):

```
== Scenario A: warn-once dedupe ==
calls=3 distinct-invalid=2 warnCount=2 (expect 2)
  sample: [telegram] Invalid allowFrom entry: "@alice" - allowFrom/groupAllowFrom authorization expects numeric Telegram sender user IDs only. To allow a T
  sample: [telegram] Invalid allowFrom entry: "@bob" - allowFrom/groupAllowFrom authorization expects numeric Telegram sender user IDs only. To allow a Tel

== Scenario B: bounded cache + eviction re-warn ==
filled 300 distinct invalid entries -> new warns=300 (expect 300)
replayed newest 256 (@user44..@user299) -> new warns=0 (expect 0: still cached & suppressed)
replayed evicted oldest (@user0) -> new warns=1 (expect 1: evicted entries warn again)

TOTAL warns=303 — bounded at 256 live keys; duplicates suppressed; eviction re-enables delivery
```

The transcript shows all three review asks against the production path: the cache stays bounded (256 live keys after 300 distinct entries), duplicate warnings stay suppressed while cached, and evicted warnings can be delivered again.

target.title: fix(ci): bound plugin-npm-release git fetch and npm publish with timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the `plugin-npm-release` workflow could remain stuck in any of its six `git fetch` steps or the `npm publish` step until the job timeout when the Git transport or npm registry stalls. This blocks plugin npm releases and wastes runner time.

## Why This Change Was Made

All six `git fetch` commands and the `npm publish` command now run through the repository's bounded process pattern: a 120-second deadline, followed by a 10-second termination grace period. This matches the pattern already applied to Mantis Crabbox workflows in #108940 (commit 16c2bbb). All release logic, merge-base checks, and non-network operations are unchanged.

The six fetch locations: extended-stable branch fetch (L134), main+release fetch (L141), alpha branch fetch (L162), source SHA fetch (L622), main fetch (L1102), and target SHA fetch (L1140). The npm publish (L1329) also receives the same timeout.

## User Impact

Maintainers get prompt, actionable failures instead of losing a plugin release runner for the full job timeout.

## Evidence

- Controlled runtime proof extracted each production workflow step, scaled the production deadline to one second, and injected a stalled transport for each network operation. Every step returned 124 in about 1.03 seconds and did not reach the five-second outer watchdog. The identical pattern was proven in #108940 and accepted in #109174.

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` passed for the changed file; `git diff --check` passed.

- The complete test suite was also attempted: all tests passed, while unrelated environment-dependent cases were skipped. The affected regression is green.

target.title: fix(models): reject oversized piped auth input
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `openclaw models auth paste-token` and `paste-api-key` accumulated piped stdin without any size limit, allowing arbitrarily large input to buffer in memory before reaching downstream validation.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `readPipedStdin()` helper now enforces a 1 MiB cap (matching the existing `MATRIX_CLI_RECOVERY_KEY_STDIN_MAX_BYTES` and `CONFIG_PATCH_STDIN_MAX_BYTES` limits). The rejection happens at the stream boundary — during the read loop, not after buffering — so oversized input never reaches auth processing.

The change follows the same buffer-chunk pattern used in the Matrix recovery-key stdin fix (PR #108120): collect `Buffer` chunks, track `totalBytes` per chunk, and throw before the cap is exceeded. Normal TTY and small piped input paths are unchanged.

Collision check: searched open PRs for `readPipedStdin`, `models auth stdin`, `paste-token unbounded` — no same-file or same-problem open PR found.

## User Impact

Piped auth commands now fail with an explicit size error for oversized input instead of buffering unbounded data. Normal interactive entry and direct arguments are unaffected.

## Evidence

Exact head: `12be34c454b75916fcf481916dec7998105820df`

### Format / diff check

```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/commands/models/auth.ts src/commands/models/auth.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ git diff --check
# exit 0
```

### Real CLI proof (local, Node 24.18.0, `pnpm dev`)

Normal small piped API key reaches auth validation:

```
$ printf 'sk-test123456789\n' | OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-test-proof     pnpm dev models auth paste-api-key --provider openai
...
Updated config: /tmp/openclaw-test-proof/openclaw.json
Auth profile: openai:manual (openai/api_key)
```

Oversized piped input (1 MiB + 1 byte) rejected at the stdin boundary:

```
$ node -e 'process.stdout.write("x".repeat(1048577))' |     OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/openclaw-test-proof     pnpm dev models auth paste-api-key --provider openai
Error: Piped auth input exceeds 1048576 bytes.
```

### Standalone proof (loopback stream, calls real production function)

```
$ node --import tsx proof-models-auth-stdin-limit.mts

  ok: small piped input does not trigger size rejection
  info: small_error=Failed to update auth profile store; ...
  ok: oversized piped input is rejected
  ok: rejection message is "Piped auth input exceeds 1048576 bytes."
  info: oversized_error=Piped auth input exceeds 1048576 bytes.

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 3 passed, 0 failed
```

### Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/models/auth.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  40 passed (40)
```

New test "rejects oversized piped auth input before buffering it" verifies the exact error message and confirms no downstream auth mutation.

### Mutation check

Reverted the fix to bare `input += String(chunk)` loop with no cap:

```
$ git checkout HEAD~1 -- src/commands/models/auth.ts
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/models/auth.test.ts
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 39 passed (40)
```

Oversized input passes through to validate() which reports "That does not look like an OpenAI API key." instead of the size rejection. Restored fix → 40/40 pass.

### Not tested

- Full `pnpm build` with dist-based CLI (Node 22.22.0 does not meet the >=22.22.3 requirement)
- The `paste-token` oversized path (shares the same `readPipedStdin` helper as the tested `paste-api-key` path)

target.title: fix(agents): avoid synthetic overflow in tool-heavy sessions
target.body:
Closes #107655

Related: #107821

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-lived, tool-heavy sessions could discard a provider-acceptable projected prompt and trigger whole-session compaction when conservative local character estimates reported pressure.

On current `main`, a restored session with twelve 50k-character tool results manufactured a local context overflow before provider submission. Recovery compacted and persistently rewrote the session even though the controlled provider accepted the projected prompt.

## Why This Change Was Made

Generic aggregate, preflight, and tool-loop character pressure now remains prompt-shaping and diagnostic input rather than proof of context overflow. Explicit opt-in mid-turn recovery remains unchanged. When a provider actually rejects context, the existing recovery path records the final provider request identity and prevents resending a byte-identical rejected payload while allowing materially changed retries.

This addresses the common false-positive authority across all three generic gates. #107821 is a useful narrow mitigation for successful aggregate replacement, but it leaves the normal preflight estimator and always-on tool-loop character guard able to manufacture the same overflow without a provider rejection.

No configuration, protocol, provider identity, public API, or persisted-session format changes.

AI-assisted: yes. I traced the runtime and upstream Codex contracts, reviewed every accepted autoreview finding, and understand the implementation and proof.

## User Impact

Tool-heavy sessions can submit their bounded provider prompt without premature compaction or history loss. Genuine provider context rejections still use bounded recovery, and an identical rejected request cannot enter a retry loop.

## Evidence

Deterministic Gateway reproduction on the current-main baseline:

- Accumulated twelve real 50k-character `exec` results under a 1.05M model window.
- Restarted the Gateway with the same model set to 272k, then sent a normal follow-up.
- Baseline made 15 provider calls, triggered synthetic compaction, and retained only 1/12 historical tool results.

Exact final patch on Blacksmith Testbox via Crabbox:

- The same real Gateway restart scenario passed in 14 provider calls.
- All 12/12 historical tool results and the newest sentinel reached the follow-up request.
- The follow-up completed without rerunning tools.
- Private reproduction harness remained under ignored `.artifacts/` and is intentionally not part of this PR.

Regression and repository proof:

- Focused prompt projection, admission, overflow, and compaction suite: 394/394 passed across 14 files.
- Fresh Codex autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings.
- `pnpm check:changed` on Testbox: passed, including production/test typechecks and full selected lint/policy gates (13m50s).
- `pnpm build` on Testbox: passed (1m22s).

target.title: fix(ci): bound docs-sync publish repo git fetch with timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The two `git fetch origin main:refs/remotes/origin/main` calls in `.github/workflows/docs-sync-publish.yml` — the stale-source check before the publish commit and the fetch inside the push retry loop — had no timeout bound. A network stall during either fetch could hang the docs publish job indefinitely, the same exposure the merged sibling fixes addressed for the publish-repo `git clone` in this file (#109173) and for `docs-agent.yml` fetches (#110026).

## Why This Change Was Made

Both fetches now run under `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=10s 120s`, the exact wrapper shape already merged for this file's clone (#109173), `docs-agent.yml` (#110026), `linux-app-release.yml` (#110027), and `macos-release.yml` (#109174). On a stall the fetch dies after 120s and the existing retry/failure logic takes over: the stale-source check already tolerates a failed fetch (it is an `if` guard), and the push loop retries with backoff and fails the job explicitly after 5 attempts instead of hanging forever.

## Changes

- Wrap both `git fetch origin main:refs/remotes/origin/main` invocations with `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=10s 120s` (2 lines).

## User Impact

A stalled GitHub network operation can no longer hang the docs publish workflow indefinitely; the job retries within bounded time or fails fast with a clear error.

## Evidence

Exact head: a6b076ffc59e7b172c20c63e945e61861b496c2d.

- Same fix shape as the merged siblings: #109173 (this file's `git clone`), #110026 (`docs-agent.yml` fetches), #110027 (`linux-app-release.yml`), #109174 (`macos-release.yml`) — identical `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=10s 120s` wrapper.
- YAML parse verified (`yaml` package): document loads, both fetch sites now carry the wrapper (count = 2).
- `git diff --check` clean.
- Existing workflow assertions pass:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run test/scripts/docs-sync-publish.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
```

- What was not tested: a live CI run (same proof scope as the merged siblings).

## Intentionally out of scope

- Other unbounded `git fetch` sites in `ci.yml` and the `mantis-*.yml` QA workflows; keeping this PR to the docs-sync-publish sibling scope of #109173.
- No change to retry counts, sleep backoff, refspecs, or failure handling.

target.title: fix(ollama): dripping model pulls hang past idle timeout during setup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where OpenClaw Ollama setup could hang forever while downloading a model when `/api/pull` kept sending occasional NDJSON progress lines that never advanced `completed`.

Affected workflow: Ollama provider setup / `ensureOllamaModelPulled` model download.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ollama setup already aborts if headers never arrive (30s) and already fails if the pull stream goes fully idle (300s). After headers return, that response timer was cleared, so only the per-chunk idle timer remained. Idle resets on every chunk, so a slow drip can keep the download alive indefinitely.

This keeps the headers and byte-idle budgets as-is, then arms a **no-progress watchdog** after the first body chunk. The watchdog resets only when aggregate Ollama `completed` increases, so duplicate non-advancing drips fail closed while monotonically advancing large/slow downloads may continue past any fixed wall-clock lifetime. Optional `streamNoProgressTimeoutMs` / `streamIdleTimeoutMs` on `ensureOllamaModelPulled` are for tests only — no new config key or env var. No new abstraction — same owner module (`pullOllamaModelCore`), same AbortController + reader cancel pattern already used for idle stalls.

ClawSweeper Maintainer option 1 applied: replaced the prior unconditional one-hour total cutoff with semantic no-progress handling.

Non-goals: changing shared `fetchWithTimeout`, remote Ollama chat streaming (`stream.ts`), or adding a hard total lifetime cap.

**Collision check:** `path:extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts` open PRs = 0 for this timeout policy. Nearby open ollama PRs touch streaming/NDJSON elsewhere, not setup pull no-progress.

## User Impact

During Ollama setup, a wedged or maliciously dripping `/api/pull` stream (bytes without advancing `completed`) fails closed with a no-progress error instead of hanging the wizard forever. Healthy pulls that keep advancing `completed` are no longer cut off by a one-hour total lifetime; true idle stalls still fail at 300s with the existing no-data message.

## Evidence

### Behavior or issue addressed

After `/api/pull` headers arrive, dripping NDJSON that resets the idle timer must still be bounded when `completed` does not advance. Advancing `completed` must be allowed past a shortened no-progress test budget.

### Canonical reachability path

Setup wizard / `ensureOllamaModelPulled` → `pullOllamaModel` → `pullOllamaModelCore` → first body chunk arms no-progress → advancing `completed` re-arms → non-advancing drip → `reader.cancel()` → no-progress error → `WizardCancelledError`.

### Focused tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ollama/src/setup.test.ts extensions/ollama/src/setup.pull.test.ts extensions/ollama/src/setup.pull-deadline.loopback.test.ts
```

```text
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  41 passed (41)
```

Coverage:
- existing idle-stall regression still green at 300s with **no data** message (empty body; no-progress not armed)
- fake-timer non-advancing drip (`streamNoProgressTimeoutMs: 1000`, idle 10s) fails with no-progress message
- fake-timer advancing `completed` continues past several shortened no-progress windows and downloads successfully
- loopback negative control: drip every 40ms + idle 100ms stays unsettled at 500ms (idle alone insufficient)
- loopback positive control: non-advancing drip + `streamNoProgressTimeoutMs: 250` rejects with no-progress message
- loopback advancing control: `completed` advances every 80ms under `streamNoProgressTimeoutMs: 250` and finishes successfully past that budget

### Real environment / loopback proof

Node local Vitest + standalone `node:http` on `127.0.0.1` only:

- **Negative idle:** idle=100ms, drip every 40ms; after 500ms still unsettled → PASS
- **No-progress drip:** timeout=250ms aborts non-advancing drip with `no progress for` stop message → PASS
- **Advancing completed:** timeout=250ms, completed +=250 every 80ms to 2000; finishes with `Downloaded gemma4` and elapsed ≥400ms → PASS

### Diff hygiene

- `oxfmt` on touched files; `git diff --check` clean
- Touched: `extensions/ollama/src/setup.ts`, `setup.test.ts`, `setup.pull.test.ts`, `setup.test-helpers.ts`, `setup.pull-deadline.loopback.test.ts`

### What was not tested

Live `ollama.com` / LAN Ollama daemon multi-hour large-model pull; controlled local drip + advancing `completed` only.

### Fix classification

bugfix — timeout/hang

### Risk / Compatibility

Low. Removes the previous unconditional one-hour total cutoff (compatibility-preserving vs that draft). Retains headers + byte-idle. Adds semantic no-progress aligned with idle budget (300s default). Test-only timeout overrides only (no new config/env). Intentional fail-closed for indefinitely non-advancing drips.

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the idle-vs-no-progress contract, first-chunk arming so empty stalls keep the no-data message, `completed`-only reset, advancing-progress regressions, loopback negative/positive/advancing controls, and proof before refresh.

target.title: fix(agents): do not treat zero-exit exec success as tool failure
target.body:
Closes #110222

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running successful exec commands (for example shellcheck reporting `SYNTAX OK`, or other zero-exit tools with short benign stdout) would still see **⚠️ Exec failed** and have `lastToolError` recorded, so the agent would treat a successful tool run as a failure and stop mid-work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Upstream tool events can set `isError=true` even when the structured result is a clear success (`exitCode: 0` / `status: completed`). Message extraction then promoted arbitrary stdout/aggregated text (including `SYNTAX OK`) into the user-visible error summary.

This PR prefers **structured success** over a misleading event-level `isError` flag when classifying tool terminal outcomes, and makes `extractToolErrorMessage` refuse to turn structured-success stdout into an error message. Genuine unstructured failures (text-only error results without structured success) still surface as errors.

Not a keyword filter on message text (that approach can hide real failures and leave the wrong classification intact).

Quality check: compatibility — no config/API shape change, same success path semantics tightened; performance — O(1) field reads on the existing tool-end path; usability — removes false-positive “Exec failed” for successful commands; security — no trust-boundary or secret handling changes.

## User Impact

Successful exec results no longer flip into false “Exec failed” / `lastToolError` state when the structured result already proves zero-exit success. Agents continue work after shellcheck-style verification chains. Real tool failures still produce error summaries.

## Evidence

Focused tests (local macOS, Crabbox not used):

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.tools.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  183 passed (183)
```

New coverage includes:

- zero-exit / `SYNTAX OK` structured success must not extract an error message
- `handleToolExecutionEnd` with `isError: true` + exitCode 0 must not set `lastToolError`
- genuine unstructured exec failures still set `lastToolError`
- `isStructuredToolSuccess` recognizes success and rejects failures/text-only errors

Static: `git diff --check` clean; `oxfmt --check` on the five touched files passed.

Live embedded agent proof (same head): two real `exec` tools in one turn — zero-exit `SYNTAX OK` with transcript `isError=false`, and exit 127 failure with `isError=true`; CLI `toolSummary` `calls=2` / `failures=1`; no `lastToolError` / `Exec failed` strings in the agent JSON output. Details in **Real behavior proof**.

Note: `pnpm check:changed` did not finish within the local closeout window; closeout used focused Vitest + path-scoped format + `git diff --check` as the quality floor for this surface.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Zero-exit exec with benign stdout (`SYNTAX OK`) must not become `lastToolError` / “Exec failed” when structured details say success; genuine unstructured failures still surface.
- Environment: local macOS, openclaw checkout at commit `f6d55afbcb` (same as this PR head). Embedded agent via `node openclaw.mjs --dev agent --local` against isolated `~/.openclaw-dev`, model `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, session `agent:main:pr-110244-proof-1784335587`, run `9344f19a-bd98-4948-9152-fe9f46068f7b`.

This branch prefers structured success for classification and refuses to promote structured-success stdout into an error message.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  ```bash
  node openclaw.mjs --dev agent \
    --local --agent main \
    --session-key agent:main:pr-110244-proof-1784335587 \
    --message-file /tmp/pr-110244-proof/message.txt \
  ```

  1. `printf 'SYNTAX OK
'; true` (zero-exit success)
  2. `sh -c 'echo command not found: shellcheck-not-installed-xyz; exit 127'` (genuine failure)

  - Agent reply:

    ```text
    SUCCESS_EXIT=0
    SUCCESS_OUT=SYNTAX OK
    FAIL_EXIT=127
    FAIL_NOTE=command 2 failed as expected with exit code 127
    ```

target.title: fix(qa-lab): unref detached qa cli child and detach stdio listeners
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runQaCli` spawns a **detached** child (non-Windows) but never `unref()`s it and never removes the `stdout`/`stderr` `data` listeners on `close`. On the success path the promise resolves while the detached process and its pipe listeners stay attached, so the parent's event loop cannot exit until the child exits.

## Why This Change Was Made

`unref()` the child after spawn so a completed qa cli run does not keep the caller alive, and remove the data listeners on `close` so the resolved stream is not retained.

## User Impact

QA Lab suite runs and the host process can exit promptly after a qa cli invocation completes; no change to success/failure behavior.

## Evidence

- Regression test "unrefs the detached child so it cannot keep the parent event loop alive": asserts `child.unref()` is called once and stdio `data` listeners are detached on `close`. **Red before the fix** (`unref` called 0 times), green after.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-process.test.ts` → 28 passed.
- Verified `upstream/main` is byte-identical for this region (not yet fixed), so this PR is not a duplicate.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: `runQaCli` in `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-process.ts` spawns a detached qa-cli child but never `unref()`s it and never removes the stdout/stderr `data` listeners on close, so the parent's event loop could stay alive (or retain the resolved stream) after the promise settles. The fix calls `child.unref()` and detaches both listeners in the `close` handler.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9. The changed spawn/unref/listener path is driven through a mocked `node:child_process` so the exact `child.unref()` call and listener detachment are asserted without spawning real processes.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-process.test.ts`

Evidence after fix (CI `Real behavior proof` job passed; local suite asserts):
```
- "unrefs the detached child so it cannot keep the parent event loop alive" -> child.unref called exactly once
- stdout/stderr data listeners removed on close so the resolved stream is not retained
```

Observed result after fix: The detached child is unref'd exactly once and both stream listeners are detached on `close`, so the caller can exit without reaping or retaining the child. The `Real behavior proof` CI check passed for this head.

What was not tested: A real subprocess spawn against a live qa-cli binary was not executed (the spawn is fully mocked); the proof targets the exact changed lines — the `unref()` call and listener cleanup — which are process-control contracts, not business logic.


---

## Test coverage

**Test file**: `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-process.test.ts`

**Changes**:
- Added `listenerCount` mock to verify listener cleanup
- Added `unref` mock to verify detached child process handling
- Tests ensure detached QA CLI child processes don't keep parent process alive

**Pattern**: Same detached process cleanup pattern used across OpenClaw test suite

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Detached qa-cli child process in `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-process.ts` was never `unref()`'d, and `data` listeners on stdout/stderr were never detached on close. Parent process could hang after the promise resolved.

**Real environment tested:** macOS 15, Node v24.18.0, vitest 4.1.9. Mocked child_process to assert exact unref/listener cleanup calls.

**Reproduction pattern before fix:**
