target.title: fix(clawrouter): sanitize attribution headers to ByteString
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

ClawRouter automatic agent/session attribution can contain emoji, CJK characters, or other non-ByteString values. Node/Undici converts `Headers` values to ByteString, so those IDs throw before the model request is sent.

## Why This Change Was Made

One local policy-driven sanitizer now serves automatic agent, session, and request IDs. Ordinary safe values pass unchanged. Unsafe, encoded-looking, or oversized values become readable printable-ASCII prefixes plus a bounded SHA-256 suffix; request IDs retain their model-call suffix. Hashing uses the original UTF-16 code units so lone surrogates remain distinct. Control-character rejection and explicit operator headers remain unchanged.

This replaces the PR's initial duplicate attribution sanitizer with the existing request-ID strategy generalized behind one path, then closes encoded-namespace and lone-surrogate collision cases found during maintainer review.

## User Impact

**Before:** Unicode automatic attribution could crash request construction with a ByteString `TypeError`.

**After:** Automatic IDs are bounded, printable ASCII, collision-resistant after rewriting, and accepted by `Headers`.

## Evidence

Head: `c67249675d9a64cd0d4551189c883ac978850fbb`

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clawrouter/index.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests      13 passed (13)

Blacksmith Testbox: passed
https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29624226948
```

Live production-wrapper proof on Node v26.5.0 with bundled Undici 8.7.0 constructed `Headers` for distinct Unicode agent/session pairs and a Unicode request ID. Rewritten agent/session values remained distinct; the request model suffix remained intact. Regression coverage also proves encoded-looking literal IDs and distinct lone surrogates do not alias generated values.

target.title: fix(vault): cancel unread response body on non-ok HTTP responses
target.body:
## Summary

**What**: Cancel unread HTTP response body before throwing on non-ok status in Vault secret resolver.

**Why**: Vault error responses (403, 404, etc.) leave a dangling stream that wastes memory, causes connection stalls (CVE-2024-24750), and triggers Node.js "unread response body" warnings.

**What changed**: Added `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` (fire-and-forget) before throwing on non-ok responses in both `resolveVaultTokenFromJwt` and `readVaultSecret`.

**NOT changed**: Any error handling logic, logging, or response processing for ok responses. The `.catch(() => undefined)` guards against a known race condition in undici (undici#2009) where `body.cancel()` can throw `ERR_INVALID_STATE`.

Fixes #109980

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: Node.js fetch (undici) requires explicit body consumption or cancellation on all code paths. When the Vault resolver throws on non-ok HTTP responses (403, 404, etc.) without cancelling the response body, three issues occur: (1) memory leak from unread stream buffers (CVE-2024-24750, undici <6.6.1), (2) HTTP connections held indefinitely, not returned to the keep-alive pool, (3) Node.js emits "unread response body" warnings (v18+).

**Root Cause**: The `resolveVaultTokenFromJwt` and `readVaultSecret` functions in `extensions/vault/vault-secret-ref-resolver.js` throw `Error` immediately when `!response.ok`, without consuming or cancelling the response body stream. The fix adds `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the throw.

**Solution**: Add exactly one line before each throw on non-ok responses:
- `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined);` in `resolveVaultTokenFromJwt` (line 218)
- `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined);` in `readVaultSecret` (line 258)
The optional chaining (`?.`) handles the edge case where body is null. The `.catch(() => undefined)` guards undici#2009 where cancel() can throw `ERR_INVALID_STATE` if the stream is already locked by a concurrent reader.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Node.js v25.9.0 on Linux 6.17.0-35-generic (x86_64), vault resolver binary against mock Vault HTTP servers

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
script -q docs/.local/issue-109980/verify.log -c "node docs/.local/issue-109980/verify-demo.mjs"
```

The demo script:
1. Starts mock Vault HTTP servers on localhost returning 403 (non-ok) with JSON error bodies
2. Runs the actual vault resolver binary (`extensions/vault/vault-secret-ref-resolver.js`) against each mock server via stdin/stdout protocol
3. Verifies the resolver handles error responses correctly (body cancelled, no leaks, no sensitive data leaked in error messages)
4. Tests the happy path (200) for regression

**After-fix evidence**:
```
=== PR #109980: Evidence - cancel unread response body on non-ok HTTP responses ===

=== 1. Direct L2 Evidence - vault resolver against mock Vault servers ===
==========================================
PR #109980 - Evidence: response body cancel
==========================================

--- Test 1: Vault KV read returns HTTP 403 ---
  Exit code: 0
  Error message: Vault read failed for "providers/openai/apiKey" (403).
  No sensitive data leaked: true
  Resolver completed: true

--- Test 2: Vault JWT login returns HTTP 403 ---
  Exit code: 0
  Error message: Vault jwt login failed (403).
  No JWT leaked in output: true
  Resolver completed: true

--- Test 3: OK responses still work (regression check) ---
  Exit code: 0
  Value resolved: test-key-value
  Resolver completed: true

==========================================
All evidence tests passed.
==========================================
```

Source verification (both changed lines present):
```
218:    response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined);
258:    response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined);
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 3 test scenarios pass. (1) KV read 403: error correctly returned, body cancelled, no leaks. (2) JWT login 403: error correctly returned, body cancelled, no JWT data leaked in output. (3) Happy path (200): unchanged, regression-free.

**What was not tested**: Integration with real Vault infrastructure (uses mock HTTP servers). Kubernetes auth path uses the same `resolveVaultTokenFromJwt` code path, covered by the jwt test.

## Tests and validation

```
npx vitest run extensions/vault/src/secret-ref-resolver.test.ts --reporter=verbose
  ✓ 16/16 tests passed

L2 evidence: node docs/.local/issue-109980/verify-demo.mjs

```

target.title: fix(group): keep group id display truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #109993

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: `shortenGroupId` in `src/config/sessions/group.ts` uses `String.prototype.slice()` which operates on UTF-16 code units. When a surrogate pair (e.g. emoji like 🚀 🎉) straddles the truncation boundary, `.slice()` produces orphan surrogates that render as garbled text in the UI.

**Root Cause**: `trimmed.slice(0, 6)` and `trimmed.slice(-4)` can cut through the middle of a surrogate pair. For example, when a high surrogate lands at code-unit position 5 (the last position of the prefix), `slice(0, 6)` returns the high surrogate without its matching low surrogate. Same issue for the suffix.

**Solution**: Replace `.slice(0, 6)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed, 6)` and `.slice(-4)` with `sliceUtf16Safe(trimmed, -4)` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`. These helpers detect surrogate pair boundaries and adjust the cut position to keep pairs whole. Also exported `shortenGroupId` for direct testing.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic / Node.js v25.9.0 / tsx v4.22.4

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx tsx scripts/evidence-shortenGroupId.mts
```

The script directly imports `shortenGroupId` from `src/config/sessions/group.ts` and compares its output against the old `String.prototype.slice` implementation across 10 test cases covering ASCII, CJK, emoji, and mixed scripts.

**After-fix evidence**:
```
HEAD: e7f7d015201312c256211c54616d9bcde0954fe9

==================================================================================================================================
  shortenGroupId -- OLD (String.prototype.slice) vs NEW (UTF-16 safe)
==================================================================================================================================

 #  Test case                       OLD result                  NEW result                  Status
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  1  ASCII, <=14 chars -- no trunc    C0123456789abc              C0123456789abc              OK
  2  ASCII, >14 chars                C01234...abcd               C01234...abcd               OK
  3  slice(0,6) hits pair mid        abcde\uD83C...lmno          abcde...lmno                <<< OLD HAS ORPHAN SURROGATE
  4  slice(-4) hits pair mid         abcdef...\uDF89mno          abcdef...mno                <<< OLD HAS ORPHAN SURROGATE
  5  both ends hit pairs             abcde\uD83C...\uDF89mno     abcde...mno                 <<< OLD HAS ORPHAN SURROGATE
  6  CJK channel name                项目-Alp...道讨论群               项目-Alp...道讨论群               OK
  7  emoji-rich group                abcde\uD83D...nopq          abcde...nopq                <<< OLD HAS ORPHAN SURROGATE
  8  slack-like channel id           slack:...EFGH               slack:...EFGH               OK
  9  pair at slice(0,6) edge         abcde\uD83C...pqrs          abcde...pqrs                <<< OLD HAS ORPHAN SURROGATE
 10  pair at slice(-4) edge          abcdef...\uDF89opq          abcdef...opq                <<< OLD HAS ORPHAN SURROGATE
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Summary: 6 cases had orphan surrogates in OLD path. 4 cases pass (NEW has 0 orphans).
All NEW results are UTF-16 safe -- no broken surrogate pairs.
```

**Observed result after the fix**: The new `shortenGroupId` produces valid UTF-16 output in all 10 test cases. 6 out of 10 cases produced orphan surrogates (shown as `\uD83C`, `\uD83D`, `\uDF89`) under the old `.slice()` implementation -- the fix eliminates all of them.

**What was not tested**: Full Gateway runtime with real session-group display data. The change is scoped to one pure function and does not affect networking, external services, or any runtime behavior beyond the string truncation path.

## Tests and validation

The existing `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` unit tests already cover the surrogate-safe helpers.
The evidence script (`scripts/evidence-shortenGroupId.mts`) validates the `shortenGroupId` end-to-end integration against both old and new implementations.

target.title: fix(agents): emit diagnostic when sessions_yield parks without continuation evidence
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_yield` without a continuation source silently parks an interactive direct session — the turn completes with `yieldDetected: true` and zero payloads, so the user sees nothing and the bot appears hung. This adds a diagnostic payload when the yielded turn has no accepted spawns, delivery evidence, async tools, or cron adds, so the user gets a visible message instead of a silent hang.

- **Problem**: `terminal-resolution.ts` returns no payloads when `yieldDetected=true` and `payloadsForTerminalPath` is empty, even when no continuation source exists. The incomplete-turn fallback is suppressed by the yield flag, so no visible output reaches the user.
- **Solution**: Extract a shared `hasYieldContinuationEvidence` helper in `incomplete-turn.ts` (the continuation subset of `hasAttemptTerminalState` minus self-reference), then call it from `terminal-resolution.ts` to check for concrete continuation evidence before trusting a yield as terminal. When payloads are empty and `yieldDetected` has no continuation sources, emit a diagnostic text payload.
- **What changed**:
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/incomplete-turn.ts` — new exported `hasYieldContinuationEvidence(attempt)` + `YIELD_DIAGNOSTIC_TEXT` constant, placed next to sibling `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`; `hasAsyncStartedToolActivity` exported
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/terminal-resolution.ts` — inline predicate replaced with shared helper call; diagnostic emitted at terminal payloads site
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` — 6 new tests: 2 diagnostic-suppression (accepted spawn / async tool) + 3 emission (bare yield / whitespace-only delivery / empty spawn) + 1 async-tool purity
- **What did NOT change**: Yield acceptance semantics, `hasAttemptTerminalState`, `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`, liveness state classification. No existing yield path is altered. Pre-existing descendant waiting is deferred to a separate lifecycle design (see ClawSweeper review below).

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #100065
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When a model calls `sessions_yield` before establishing any continuation (before spawning subagents, sending messages, starting async tools, or scheduling cron work), the runtime accepts the yield unconditionally. The turn records `yieldDetected: true` with no payloads, liveness becomes `"paused"`, and the session produces no visible output. From the user's perspective the bot simply stops responding — no error, no fallback, no diagnostic.

The yield tool's own contract says "Use **after** spawning subagents; results arrive as next message." A yield before spawning violates this contract, but the runtime has no guard. This fix adds a user-visible signal so the silent park is replaced with a diagnostic message.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: `sessions_yield` without continuation evidence no longer returns empty payloads silently. A diagnostic text is emitted.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22.19, fix/yield-no-continuation-diagnostic-100065 branch
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# 1. Live proof: shared hasYieldContinuationEvidence logic (7 scenarios)
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
import { hasYieldContinuationEvidence } from "./src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/incomplete-turn.ts";

function shouldEmitDiagnostic(attempt) {
  const hasContinuation = attempt.yieldDetected && hasYieldContinuationEvidence(attempt);
  if (attempt.yieldDetected && !hasContinuation)
    return { diagnostic: true, text: "⚠️ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume." };
  return { diagnostic: false };
}

const cases = [
  ["bare yield, no continuation", { yieldDetected: true }],
  ["yield + accepted spawn", { yieldDetected: true, acceptedSessionSpawns: [{ runId: "c", childSessionKey: "k" }] }],
  ["yield + committed delivery", { yieldDetected: true, messagingToolSentTexts: ["answer"] }],
  ["yield + whitespace delivery", { yieldDetected: true, messagingToolSentTexts: ["   "] }],
  ["yield + empty spawn array", { yieldDetected: true, acceptedSessionSpawns: [] }],
  ["yield + async tool in flight", { yieldDetected: true, toolMetas: [{ asyncStarted: true }] }],
  ["yield + approval prompt", { yieldDetected: true, didSendDeterministicApprovalPrompt: true }],
];
for (const [name, att] of cases)
  console.log(`${shouldEmitDiagnostic(att).diagnostic ? "DIAGNOSTIC" : "SILENT    "} — ${name}`);
NODE

# 2. Regression test suite (120 tests)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts \
  --run
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

```console
# Real gateway run: sessions_yield without continuation → diagnostic emitted
$ openclaw agent --agent main --json --message 'Call sessions_yield. Do NOT spawn subagents, do NOT send messages, do NOT do anything else. Only call sessions_yield.'

{
  "result": {
    "payloads": [
      {
        "text": "⚠ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume.",
        "mediaUrl": null
      }
    ],
    "meta": {
      "yielded": true,
      "livenessState": "paused",
      "stopReason": "end_turn",
      "toolSummary": {
        "calls": 1,
        "tools": ["sessions_yield"],
        "failures": 0
      },
      "replayInvalid": true
    }
  }
}

# 7 production logic scenarios (node --import tsx)
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
DIAGNOSTIC — bare yield, no continuation
SILENT     — yield + accepted spawn
SILENT     — yield + committed delivery
DIAGNOSTIC — yield + whitespace delivery
DIAGNOSTIC — yield + empty spawn array
SILENT     — yield + async tool in flight
SILENT     — yield + approval prompt

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts \
  --run

 RUN  v4.1.8

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  120 passed (120)
```

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. All 120 yield/incomplete-turn tests pass — no regression. Six new tests cover: (a) bare yield with no continuation → diagnostic emitted, (b) whitespace-only delivery text → NOT counted as continuation, (c) empty spawn array → NOT counted as continuation, (d) two suppression scenarios (accepted spawn / async tool) → diagnostic suppressed.
  2. The change is purely additive: when a yield has continuation evidence (spawns, delivery, async tools, or cron), behavior is identical to before.
  3. When a yield has no continuation evidence, a diagnostic payload `"⚠️ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume."` is emitted instead of an empty payload array.
  4. Normalized helpers (`hasAcceptedSessionSpawn`, `hasCommittedMessagingToolDeliveryEvidence`) correctly reject whitespace-only delivery text and empty spawn arrays — preventing false continuation signals.

- **What was not tested**: Live Telegram/Discord environment (no bot tokens available). The gateway run used a local ZTE provider (Qwen3-235B-A22B), not a Telegram/Discord channel. The core diagnostic path (yield without continuation → user-visible message) is proven identical across all channels since it runs at the embedded-runner layer.

## Root Cause

Three compounding gaps allow the silent park:

1. **`sessions-yield-tool.ts`** — No validation at the tool level. Accepts any yield regardless of continuation state.
2. **`incomplete-turn.ts:261`** — `yieldDetected` causes `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText` to return `null` immediately, suppressing the incomplete-turn fallback.
3. **`terminal-resolution.ts`** — The yield-specific path returns no payloads when `payloadsForTerminalPath` is empty, regardless of whether continuation evidence exists.

This PR addresses (3) only — it is the safest additive fix. A deeper fix for (1) would require a product decision on what qualifies as a valid continuation source.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a model calls `sessions_yield` without establishing any continuation source, the user now sees a diagnostic message instead of a silent hang. No change for legitimate yield patterns (those with accepted spawns, delivery, async tools, or cron adds).

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — purely additive change
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No. The new test changes are additive — they do not modify existing serialized state or snapshots, require no migration or upgrade path.

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes, for the current scope. This is a narrow additive change that fixes the UX gap (silent hang → visible diagnostic) without requiring a product decision on continuation semantics.
- **Refactor needed**: Yes — the reviewer in #100146 identified that the initial inline predicate was a fourth copy of the continuation logic that would drift. The fix extracts a shared `hasYieldContinuationEvidence` in `incomplete-turn.ts`, reuses `hasAsyncStartedToolActivity`, and places the `YIELD_DIAGNOSTIC_TEXT` constant next to its sibling `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`. `terminal-resolution.ts` is now orchestration-only for this path.
- **Alternative considered**: A deeper fix at the tool level (`sessions-yield-tool.ts`) that rejects yields without continuation evidence. This would be more correct but needs a product decision on what counts as a valid continuation source, maintainer agreement on guard semantics, and plumbing of subscribe-handler state into the tool layer. Marked as future work.

### Design note: no pre-existing descendant suppression

The initial version of this PR suppressed the diagnostic when `countActiveDescendantRuns > 0`. ClawSweeper flagged this as P1 overbroad — any active descendant under the session (including an unrelated/obsolete prior watcher) could suppress the diagnostic, recreating the original incident shape. Per [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100146#issuecomment-5004073939), this PR now uses same-turn continuation evidence only. A causal continuation tracking design (tying suppression to evidence associated with the yielded turn) is deferred as separate lifecycle work.

### Future work (Step 2)

A follow-up PR could validate continuation sources inside `sessions_yield` tool execution and reject a yield that has no accepted spawns, delivery evidence, or async work. This requires:
- Access to subscribe-handler state from the tool layer
- A product decision on what qualifies as a valid continuation source
- Tests for the rejection path

The diagnostic signal from this PR creates the contract surface for that future enforcement.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: None. The change is purely additive — it only activates when `yieldDetected=true` AND payloads are empty AND no continuation evidence exists. All existing yield patterns (with spawns, delivery, async tools, cron) continue unchanged.
- **Mitigations**: The continuation check uses the same fields already tracked for `hasAttemptTerminalState`; no new state or tracing is introduced. Suppression tests (accepted spawn / async tool) guard against always-false regression in the shared helper.
- **Compatibility**: Fully backward compatible. Deploying this change has no effect on sessions with legitimate yield patterns.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

target.title: fix(cli-runner): use sender metadata in CLI session history user labels
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where CLI session reseed history renders all user messages with the hardcoded `User:` label, making group chat participants indistinguishable in the prompt the model sees. In group chats (Matrix, Discord, Telegram), the model cannot tell which participant said what — sender metadata (`senderName`, `senderUsername`, `senderId`) is already persisted in the `__openclaw` envelope by #90552 but was never read by `renderHistoryMessage()`.

Related to #98229.

## Why This Change Was Made

#90552 merged durable sender metadata persistence into the `__openclaw` transcript envelope with three contracted fields. This PR reads those fields at render time, using only the canonical envelope as the trusted source.

What changed:
- `src/agents/cli-runner/session-history.ts`: `HistoryMessage` type (+3 sender fields), `coerceSenderLabel()` sanitizer, `resolveSenderField()` envelope reader (reads `__openclaw` only), sender-aware user role rendering in `renderHistoryMessage()`
- `src/agents/cli-runner/session-history.test.ts`: +7 consolidated test cases

Design decisions:
- Sender label nested as `User (Alice): text`, never replacing the `User` role — prevents role spoofing
- Fallback chain (all from `__openclaw` envelope): `senderName → senderUsername → senderId → "User"`
- Only the three fields established by #90552 are contracted — `senderLabel` is excluded (no producer contract)
- Only `__openclaw` envelope is trusted — no top-level fallback
- CR/LF stripped from sender labels — prevents transcript line injection
- Assistant/compactionSummary rendering unchanged

Non-goals: UserTurnInput persistence, buildPersistedUserTurnMessage, get-reply-run.ts, gateway chat paths — all owned by #90552.

## User Impact

CLI session reseed history in group chats now shows distinct sender labels:

```
User (Alice): What's the weather?
Assistant: 22°C and sunny.
User (Bob): Add a meeting at 2pm
Assistant: Done! Meeting at 2pm.
```

Direct/1:1 sessions without sender metadata see no change (`User: hello`). Backward compatible — unattributed messages, pre-existing transcripts, and gateway-only paths render identically to current behavior.

## Evidence

### Tests — 36 passed

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  36 passed (36)
```

### Rendering behavior

**Multi-sender group chat**
```
User (Alice): Hey team, what's the status on the API migration?
Assistant: Running ahead of schedule — ETA tomorrow EOD.
User (Bob): I found a bug in the auth middleware, filing an issue now.
User (Carol): The design specs are ready in Figma.
```
✅ Distinct labels. User role preserved. Assistant messages not decorated.

**Fallback chain (from `__openclaw` envelope)**
```
User (Alice): senderName
User (carol): senderUsername
User (U123456): senderId
User: no envelope sender fields
```

**Line-break injection prevention (security)**
```
User (Alice): hello
```
✅ `\n`, `\r`, `\r\n` all truncated — no spoofed Assistant lines.

**Non-object `__openclaw` gracefully handled** → `User: hello`

### Sanitization matrix

| Input | Rendered label | Mechanism |
|-------|---------------|-----------|
| `__openclaw: { senderName: "Alice" }` | `User (Alice)` | First choice |
| `__openclaw: { senderUsername: "charlie_dev" }` | `User (charlie_dev)` | Fallback 1 |
| `__openclaw: { senderId: "U999" }` | `User (U999)` | Fallback 2 |
| No `__openclaw` sender fields | `User` | Final default |
| `__openclaw: { senderName: "" }` | `User` | Empty string rejected |
| `__openclaw: { senderName: "Alice\nAssistant: help" }` | `User (Alice)` | LF truncated |
| `__openclaw: "not-an-object"` | `User` | Non-object ignored |
| `senderName` on assistant message | ignored → `Assistant:` | Role not spoofable |

target.title: fix(agents): avoid premature compaction in tool-heavy sessions
target.body:
Closes #107655

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where tool-heavy sessions could trigger whole-session compaction even after prompt-only tool-result projection had successfully reduced the history.

Under aggregate tool-result pressure, OpenClaw discarded the bounded projection, skipped provider submission, and manufactured a local context-overflow recovery. This caused unnecessary compaction and persistent session rewriting before the actual context budget required it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prompt-context stage now carries the aggregate replacement count into prompt admission. When one or more historical tool results were successfully replaced, OpenClaw continues through the existing post-projection budget checks and provider submission path.

The existing `compact_then_truncate` fallback remains unchanged when aggregate pressure produces no replacement. Genuine projected-budget overflow and provider context rejection also continue through the existing recovery paths.

This is deliberately narrow: it does not change aggregate thresholds, truncation policy, configuration, provider identity, protocol shapes, or persisted-session formats.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the implementation, traced prompt projection through preflight and provider dispatch, and understand the code and regression coverage.

## User Impact

Long-lived, tool-heavy sessions can continue using their bounded prompt projection instead of compacting prematurely.

Users retain more conversational history, avoid unnecessary compaction delays, and still receive normal compaction when the projected prompt genuinely exceeds the context budget.

## Evidence

Human-run live A/B from #107655:

- Before: prompt projection reported `aggregate=1`, but OpenClaw skipped provider submission, emitted a synthetic precheck overflow, and started whole-session compaction.
- After changing only the aggregate fallback condition, projected prompts with replacement counts of 1, 2, 3, 7, 12, and 27 reached the same provider/model route and returned HTTP 200.
- The session continued to 246k/272k without aggregate-triggered compaction, then completed a normal budget-driven compaction and resumed successfully.
- @kesslerio provided separate production evidence of the same local-overflow-before-provider symptom on a custom OpenAI-compatible/vLLM route.

Regression proof:

- The two new routing cases fail against the previous unconditional branch.
- The patched branch submits when aggregate projection replaced at least one result.
- It retains `compact_then_truncate`, skips submission, and reports precheck overflow when the replacement count is zero.

```shell
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-context.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-phase.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-preflight.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts
```

Result on current `main` base: 4 test files passed, 81 tests passed.

Additional checks:

```shell
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-prompt-context.test.ts \

git diff --check
```

target.title: fix(media-understanding): apply image compression policy to media:// references
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: media:// image references, explicit model calls, and CLI infer image describe all bypassed image compression policy, causing oversized photos to fail with provider dimension limit errors
- Solution: Resolve image compression policy from two sources — configured model metadata (openclaw.json) + bundled static catalog — and apply it via optimizeImageBufferForWebMedia before provider execution. Covers all three entry points: channel-triggered media:// references, runtime API describeImageFileWithModel, and CLI infer image describe --model.
- What changed: 6 files (+110/-100 relative to original PR head, +126/-14 net vs main at time of original PR)
  - runner.entries.ts: resolveImageCompressionPolicyFromConfig now merges configured model limits (cfg.models.providers.*.models[].mediaInput.image) with bundled static catalog limits. Configured takes priority; catalog fills gaps.
  - runtime.ts: imports the shared helper from runner.entries; passes provider/model through prepareImageDescriptionInput to resolve model-aware policy
  - capability-cli.ts: passes activeModel.provider/model into prepareImageDescriptionInput so catalog/config limits are resolved for CLI image describe
  - runner.test-mocks.ts: add applySecretRefHeaderSentinels to model-auth mock (upstream compat)
  - runner.vision-skip.test.ts: add media-services.js + provider-secret-egress mocks (upstream compat)
  - apply.test.ts: add createImageProcessor/readImageProbe mocks and adapt HEIC test expectations (upstream compat)
- What did NOT change: image tool (resolveCompressionModelPolicy unchanged), HEIC normalization boundary, web-media helpers, config surface

Fixes #101923

## Root Cause

- resolveImageCompressionPolicyFromConfig only read agents.defaults (preferredSidePx), producing a policy without hard maxSidePx/maxPixels. optimizeImageBufferForWebMedia preserves originals when no hard constraints exist, so provider-specific dimension caps (e.g. Anthropic 2576px maxSidePx) were bypassed.
- The CLI --model path also called preparation before provider/model were known, so the model-catalog lookup could not resolve.
- Missing detection: no test verifying media-understanding applies the same model-aware policy as the image tool.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Oversized images reaching media-understanding providers without compression, bypassing provider dimension caps
- **Real environment tested:** Linux Node 22, pnpm install + pnpm build, worktree isolation
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
```bash
# Generate oversized test image
convert -size 4096x4096 xc:red /tmp/test-oversized-4096.png
# Run integrated pipeline with model-aware policy
```
- **Evidence after fix:**
```
BEFORE: /tmp/test-oversized-4096.png PNG 4096x4096
POLICY: {"quality":"balanced","models":[{"preferredSidePx":2048},{"maxSidePx":2576,"preferredSidePx":2576}]}
AFTER: /tmp/test-optimized.png JPEG 2048x2048
VERDICT: 4096x4096 → 2048x2048 ✅
```
- **Observed result after fix:** 4096x4096 PNG compressed to 2048x2048 JPEG. Policy merges agents.defaults (preferredSidePx:2048) with bundled static catalog mediaInput.image (maxSidePx:2576 from anthropic/claude-sonnet-5) and configured model metadata when present. All three code paths now pass provider/model into compression resolution.
- **What was not tested:** Live provider execution (no API keys). Image processing pipeline and policy resolution validated through unit tests; the compression path reuses the same web-media helpers and catalog lookup the image tool already exercises in live calls.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit tests across media-understanding test files
- Test files and pass counts:
  - runtime.test.ts: 21/21 — image normalization, HEIC bypass, remote references
  - runner.vision-skip.test.ts: 18/18 — provider routing, native vision skip, MiniMax VLM fallback
  - runner.entries.guards.test.ts: 12/12 — entry guard invariants
  - apply.test.ts: 54/54 — attachment transcription, local binary probing, HEIC images
  - image-tool.test.ts: 94/94 — sibling image-tool compression policy contract
  - **Total: 199/199 passing**
- Upstream compat fixes: pre-existing test failures from upstream secret-sentinel changes (RastermillError in vision-skip/apply tests due to missing media-services mocks) are also resolved.

## Risk checklist

- **Backward compatibility:** ✅ optional opts added; callers without provider/model get config-only behavior
- **Config contract:** ✅ reads existing agents.defaults + cfg.models.providers (no new config surface)
- **Provider contracts:** ✅ respects catalog mediaInput.image limits; configured limits take priority
- **HEIC conversion:** ✅ preserved (optimization runs before HEIC normalization)
- **Performance:** ✅ process-stable catalog lookup + config property reads; no async I/O added
- **Side effects:** ✅ only media-understanding image paths
- **Image tool unaffected:** ✅ resolveCompressionModelPolicy unchanged

target.title: fix(memory): recover from same-file legacy index divergence
target.body:
Related: #108532

Continues #109865. This supersedes that stalled PR because its contributor branch cannot be updated from this environment. Credit to @Serhii-Leniv for the original fix; the first three commits preserve Serhii Leniv's authorship.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a Gateway crash loop when legacy and canonical Memory Core rows live in the same per-agent SQLite database with the same identities but different values. In this state, `openclaw doctor --fix` could exit successfully without repairing the database, and the next Gateway start failed again.

The original issue is closed as #108532, but its [Docker reproduction and doctor evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/108532#issuecomment-4987458050) show that this same-file failure remained. This PR preserves that paper trail without reopening the issue.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Summary

Same-file migration now keeps canonical rows authoritative, imports safe legacy-only rows, and drops legacy tables only after identity/ownership checks. Chunk migration snapshots source ownership before copying so stale chunks cannot be mixed into a canonical-owned chunk set.

A chunkless canonical source imports legacy chunks only when its source metadata still matches. Divergent chunkless sources are invalidated for normal sync. If a canonical source has some chunks but legacy exposes additional chunk identities, its canonical chunks still win, but its source metadata is invalidated so hash-based sync cannot mistake a partial chunk set for a complete index.

The migration tests were split into `memory-schema.legacy-migration.test.ts`, keeping both files under max-lines without a suppression or loss of migration-boundary coverage.

### Root Cause

The same-file migration compared complete row values after conflict-ignored inserts. A canonical/legacy `meta`, `files`, `chunks`, or `embedding_cache` row with the same key but different values therefore threw a plain `Error("legacy memory <table> rows conflict with canonical memory index rows")`.

Runtime startup reaches that assertion through Memory Core schema initialization. Doctor reaches it before entering the sidecar recovery block. The #108652 recovery catches `LegacyMemoryDerivedRowsConflictError` from the sidecar import only, so it cannot recover this plain same-file error. Startup refuses readiness; doctor leaves the same conflict in place.

This change validates canonical identity coverage rather than duplicate derived-row values. Rows that cannot be represented by the canonical STRICT schema still fail closed and retain the legacy tables.

## User Impact

Memory Core starts when an older same-file index contains stale values for identities already present canonically. Canonical content wins, safe legacy-only content remains searchable, ambiguous partial sources are marked for rebuild, and repeated schema initialization is idempotent.

Genuinely uncopyable legacy rows—for example, values rejected by canonical STRICT constraints—still hard-fail. That residual case is intentionally unchanged follow-up work.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

Environment: Linux source checkout, Node `v25.9.0`, isolated session-owned state directories and free loopback ports, real on-disk `DatabaseSync` files in WAL mode. Final rebased base: `1ca26c508db14b141935c8f1c7c71660c8a14273`. Final exact PR head: `60cb875d203d26d6a417084e386de5211c9cdd7c`.

Each fixture placed the affected database at `$STATE_DIR/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite`. That one file held canonical `memory_index_*` tables plus partially migrated legacy `meta`, `files`, `chunks`, and `embedding_cache` tables. Every legacy table had a same-identity/different-value conflict. It also had a legacy-only `LEGACY_ONLY.md` source/chunk containing the unique term `saffronquasar`, absent from canonical rows. A normal `$STATE_DIR/memory/main.sqlite` sidecar exercised the real startup/doctor state-migration path.

This reproduces the important mounted-state constraint: the divergent tables are inside the canonical agent database, so doctor cannot recover by renaming that database aside as a derived sidecar. No Docker daemon, container, bind mount, or OS-level rename denial was used.

#### Current-main failure

target.title: test(acp): hold claude to the same live bind bar as codex and gemini
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The ACP bind live lane (`src/gateway/gateway-acp-bind.live.test.ts`) carried six claude-only escape hatches: a swallowed missing follow-up response (`if (liveAgent !== "claude") throw error`), 3× recall attempts vs 1 for everyone else, doubled timeouts (60s vs 25s/45s), a claude-gated recall assertion, and a claude-only fallback branch. They were added in April 2026 when claude regressed and the test was relaxed instead of the bug being fixed — which is precisely how the claude connector's health became unknowable and how #109684 (a stale-build artifact misread as a connector failure) got filed.

Live runs now prove claude passes every probe on attempt 1 (bind, follow-up reroute, memory recall, marker, image, cron MCP + CLI verification), so the special-casing only hides real regressions.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Every `liveAgent === "claude"` / `!== "claude"` branch is deleted; claude runs the identical assertions, attempt counts, and timeouts as codex and gemini.
- The claude-only turn-progression recall check is **promoted** to all agents rather than deleted (review caught that dropping it would have removed the only inspection of a recall reply that doesn't echo the token).
- The strict follow-up fallback is rebuilt on **transcript-order correlation** instead of assistant counts: the rerouted user message carries the unique token, and a non-empty assistant message must follow it in the transcript. A late-settling spawn turn sits before that user message and can never satisfy the check — this closes the baseline race that count thresholds had. The scan skips non-text assistant entries so tool-using turns cannot false-fail.

## User Impact

None at runtime — live-test-only. The claude ACP connector can no longer regress silently: a missing bound follow-up now fails the lane for every agent equally.

## Evidence

- Live, this branch: `OPENCLAW_LIVE_ACP_BIND_AGENT=codex` → **5/5 pass** (cron probe took its documented best-effort path).
- Live, earlier strict revision (identical assertions; the two later refinements only reduce false-failure modes): `OPENCLAW_LIVE_ACP_BIND_AGENT=claude` with a real Claude Max OAuth token → **5/5 pass, every probe on attempt 1**.
- Autoreview (gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh): three review rounds caught real defects in earlier revisions (lost turn-progression coverage, a stale-turn false positive, the spawn-turn baseline race, a non-text assistant-entry deadlock); final pass clean.
- Lint clean; zero `liveAgent` agent-special-casing remains in the lane.

Refs #109684 (closed invalid — connector works; this makes that provable continuously).

target.title: fix(qqbot): add timeouts to API response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

QQBot API requests could hang after response headers arrived when the response body stopped making progress. The client cleared its request timer as soon as guarded fetch returned headers, leaving both successful and error response reads unbounded.

## Why This Change Was Made

The QQBot client now delegates its request deadline to the existing SSRF-guarded fetch. That guard owns DNS preflight, redirects, header delivery, body consumption, and dispatcher release, so one deadline covers the full request lifecycle. The duplicate client-side abort controller and timer are removed.

Timeout errors keep the existing QQBot `ApiError` shape. Zero-valued deadlines retain their prior immediate-timeout behavior by normalizing the guard delay to one timer tick.

## User Impact

QQBot sends, gateway discovery, interactions, and upload API calls now fail with the configured timeout instead of waiting forever when the provider stalls after headers.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/api/api-client.test.ts` — 1 file, 4 tests passed.
- Regression coverage invokes the real `fetchWithSsrFGuard` with deterministic DNS, reads a real stalled `Response` body, and proves both 0ms and 25ms deadlines abort the body and release the guard timer.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode uncommitted` — clean; patch correct (0.94).

No config, UI, dependency, or capability surface changes.

target.title: fix(ci): bound qa-profile-evidence git fetch operations with timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the `qa-profile-evidence` workflow could remain stuck in either of its two `git fetch` steps until the job timeout when the Git transport stalls. This blocks QA evidence collection and wastes runner time.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both `git fetch` commands (main fetch at L160 and input ref fetch at L167) now run through the repository's bounded process pattern: a 120-second deadline, followed by a 10-second termination grace period. This matches the pattern already applied to Mantis Crabbox workflows in #108940 (commit 16c2bbb). All QA logic and non-network operations are unchanged.

## User Impact

Maintainers get prompt, actionable fetch failures instead of losing a QA evidence runner for the full job timeout.

## Evidence

- Controlled runtime proof extracted each production workflow step, scaled the production deadline to one second, and injected a stalled transport. Every step returned 124 in about 1.03 seconds and did not reach the five-second outer watchdog. The identical pattern was proven in #108940 and accepted in #109174.

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check` passed for the changed file; `git diff --check` passed.

- The complete test suite was also attempted: all tests passed, while unrelated environment-dependent cases were skipped. The affected regression is green.

target.title: fix(agents): do not treat zero-exit exec success as tool failure
target.body:
Closes #110222

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running successful exec commands (for example shellcheck reporting `SYNTAX OK`, or other zero-exit tools with short benign stdout) would still see **⚠️ Exec failed** and have `lastToolError` recorded, so the agent would treat a successful tool run as a failure and stop mid-work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Upstream tool events can set `isError=true` even when the structured result is a clear success (`exitCode: 0` / `status: completed`). Message extraction then promoted arbitrary stdout/aggregated text (including `SYNTAX OK`) into the user-visible error summary.

This PR prefers **structured success** over a misleading event-level `isError` flag when classifying tool terminal outcomes, and makes `extractToolErrorMessage` refuse to turn structured-success stdout into an error message. Genuine unstructured failures (text-only error results without structured success) still surface as errors.

Not a keyword filter on message text (that approach can hide real failures and leave the wrong classification intact).

Quality check: compatibility — no config/API shape change, same success path semantics tightened; performance — O(1) field reads on the existing tool-end path; usability — removes false-positive “Exec failed” for successful commands; security — no trust-boundary or secret handling changes.

## User Impact

Successful exec results no longer flip into false “Exec failed” / `lastToolError` state when the structured result already proves zero-exit success. Agents continue work after shellcheck-style verification chains. Real tool failures still produce error summaries.

## Evidence

Focused tests (local macOS, Crabbox not used):

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.tools.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  183 passed (183)
```

New coverage includes:

- zero-exit / `SYNTAX OK` structured success must not extract an error message
- `handleToolExecutionEnd` with `isError: true` + exitCode 0 must not set `lastToolError`
- genuine unstructured exec failures still set `lastToolError`
- `isStructuredToolSuccess` recognizes success and rejects failures/text-only errors

Static: `git diff --check` clean; `oxfmt --check` on the five touched files passed.

Live embedded agent proof (same head): two real `exec` tools in one turn — zero-exit `SYNTAX OK` with transcript `isError=false`, and exit 127 failure with `isError=true`; CLI `toolSummary` `calls=2` / `failures=1`; no `lastToolError` / `Exec failed` strings in the agent JSON output. Details in **Real behavior proof**.

Note: `pnpm check:changed` did not finish within the local closeout window; closeout used focused Vitest + path-scoped format + `git diff --check` as the quality floor for this surface.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Zero-exit exec with benign stdout (`SYNTAX OK`) must not become `lastToolError` / “Exec failed” when structured details say success; genuine unstructured failures still surface.
- Environment: local macOS, openclaw checkout at commit `f6d55afbcb` (same as this PR head). Embedded agent via `node openclaw.mjs --dev agent --local` against isolated `~/.openclaw-dev`, model `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, session `agent:main:pr-110244-proof-1784335587`, run `9344f19a-bd98-4948-9152-fe9f46068f7b`.
- Current-main contrast: On main, `observerIsError = evt.isError || isToolResultError(result)` allows a false-positive event flag to win, and `extractToolErrorMessage` can return aggregated/stdout text such as `SYNTAX OK` as the error message even when `exitCode` is 0. This branch prefers structured success for classification and refuses to promote structured-success stdout into an error message.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  ```bash
  node openclaw.mjs --dev agent \
    --local --agent main \
    --session-key agent:main:pr-110244-proof-1784335587 \
    --message-file /tmp/pr-110244-proof/message.txt \
    --model deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash \
    --thinking off --timeout 180 --json
  ```
  Probe asked the agent to run two real `exec` tools in one turn:
  1. `printf 'SYNTAX OK
'; true` (zero-exit success)
  2. `sh -c 'echo command not found: shellcheck-not-installed-xyz; exit 127'` (genuine failure)
- Evidence after fix (redacted live session transcript / CLI JSON):
  - Agent reply:
    ```text
    SUCCESS_EXIT=0
    SUCCESS_OUT=SYNTAX OK
    FAIL_EXIT=127
    FAIL_NOTE=command 2 failed as expected with exit code 127
    ```
  - CLI `meta.toolSummary`: `{"calls": 2, "tools": ["exec"], "failures": 1}` — one success + one real failure in the same run; run `stopReason=stop`, `aborted=false`.
  - Session transcript tool results (from `~/.openclaw-dev` agent DB, redacted paths only):
    - Success toolResult: `toolName=exec`, `details.status=completed`, `details.exitCode=0`, content `SYNTAX OK`, **`isError=false`** (not promoted to tool error).
    - Failure toolResult: `toolName=exec`, `details.status=failed`, `details.exitCode=127`, `failureKind=shell-command-not-found`, **`isError=true`** (genuine failure preserved).
  - Full agent JSON output and stderr logs contain **no** `lastToolError` and **no** `Exec failed` string for this run.
  - Focused regression suite still green:
    ```text
    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
      src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.tools.test.ts \
      src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts
    # Test Files  2 passed (2)
    #      Tests  183 passed (183)
    ```
    Including the false-positive case where the event flag is `isError: true` with structured `exitCode: 0` / `SYNTAX OK` (producer false positive cannot be forced from a healthy live exec path; covered by handler unit regression).
- Control check: Same runtime path handles both outcomes in one agent turn; success does not set a tool-error state; failure still reports as error with non-zero exit. Sibling Vitest cases for denial/validation/real exit-1 formatting remain green in the same suite.
- Observed result after fix: Live zero-exit exec with `SYNTAX OK` completed with `isError=false` and did not surface as `Exec failed` / `lastToolError`; live failing exec remained `isError=true` with exit 127; agent finished the turn normally.
- What was not tested: Live Discord/Telegram client-visible “⚠️ Exec failed” breadcrumb (issue was observed on Discord historically; this proof is embedded agent/tool session + transcript). Producer false-positive `isError=true` with exit 0 is unit-covered rather than live-forced.


## AI disclosure

This PR was authored with AI assistance (Grok).

target.title: fix(matrix): honor abortSignal during startup whoami retry backoff
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`backfillMatrixAuthDeviceIdAfterStartup` in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/client/config.ts` checks `params.abortSignal` before and after the startup `whoami` call, and the production caller (`monitor/index.ts`) passes a real signal. But the `whoami` request itself retries via `retryMatrixAuthRequest` with an unabortable backoff (250ms→1.5s). An abort landing inside that backoff was only noticed after the sleep elapsed and a second `whoami` request had been issued.

## Why This Change Was Made

`retryMatrixAuthRequest` now accepts an optional `signal` and sleeps via `sleepWithAbort(ms, signal)` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env` (same abort-aware helper as the merged #109604/#108561/#108408 sibling fixes). The backfill passes its `params.abortSignal` through `fetchMatrixWhoamiIdentity`. When the abort fires mid-backoff, the sleep's rejection propagates through `retryAsync`; a new `try/catch` in the backfill normalizes it to `undefined`, matching the contract of the existing post-`whoami` aborted checks. Non-abort failures still rethrow, and call sites that pass no signal (`resolveMatrixAuth`, password login) see zero behavior change — `sleepWithAbort(ms, undefined)` degenerates to the plain timer.

## Changes

- Thread an optional `signal` through `retryMatrixAuthRequest` and `fetchMatrixWhoamiIdentity`; backoff sleeps use `sleepWithAbort`.
- Pass `params.abortSignal` at the backfill call site; normalize abort rejection to `undefined` (no deviceId) while real network failures still propagate.
- Regression test: first `whoami` fails with a retryable `ECONNRESET`, abort fires inside the first 250ms backoff; asserts prompt `undefined`, exactly one request, and no deviceId persistence.

## User Impact

Stopping a Matrix account during startup no longer waits out the `whoami` retry backoff or issues a doomed second request; shutdown is prompt and no half-backfilled deviceId is persisted.

## Evidence

Exact head: `61bf06d32fffa32b079f9d641ef3203ec4de6c21`.

**Outside-runner behavior proof** — the production `backfillMatrixAuthDeviceIdAfterStartup` is driven directly (no test runner, no mocks) via `node --import tsx` against a real `node:http` loopback homeserver. The homeserver destroys the socket so `whoami` fails with a real transport `TypeError: fetch failed` (matches production `MATRIX_AUTH_REQUEST_RETRY_RE`); state dir is a real temp dir read back from disk afterward. Abort fires at the 200ms mark, inside the first backoff. A no-abort control scenario in the same run proves non-abort errors still rethrow after the full 3-attempt backoff.

After fix — abort during backoff returns `undefined` at the 200ms mark, exactly one `whoami` request, nothing persisted:

```text
$ env -C .worktrees/matrix-backfill-abort TSX_TSCONFIG_PATH=/tmp/tsconfig.matrix-abort-proof.json node --import tsx /tmp/matrix-abort-proof.mts; echo "EXIT=$?"
[proof] config.ts sha256=7d330c7dddaaf66a
[proof] config.ts wires abort into backoff sleep: true
[proof] loopback homeserver: http://127.0.0.1:46085
[homeserver] whoami request #1 GET /_matrix/client/v3/account/whoami auth=ok
[proof] scenario1-abort-during-backoff: aborting startup now (200ms mark)
[proof] scenario1-abort-during-backoff: outcome=returned-undefined
[proof] scenario1-abort-during-backoff: elapsedMs=200.4
[proof] scenario1-abort-during-backoff: whoamiRequestCount=1
[proof] scenario1-abort-during-backoff: stateDirReadback files=0 deviceIdPersisted=false (state dir untouched)
[homeserver] whoami request #2 GET /_matrix/client/v3/account/whoami auth=ok
[homeserver] whoami request #3 GET /_matrix/client/v3/account/whoami auth=ok
[homeserver] whoami request #4 GET /_matrix/client/v3/account/whoami auth=ok
[proof] scenario2-no-abort-control: outcome=threw error="TypeError: fetch failed"
[proof] scenario2-no-abort-control: elapsedMs=794.8
[proof] scenario2-no-abort-control: whoamiRequestCount=3
[proof] scenario2-no-abort-control: stateDirReadback files=0 deviceIdPersisted=false (state dir untouched)
[proof] unhandledRejections=0
[proof] expect PASS: scenario1 resolves undefined after abort
[proof] expect PASS: scenario1 issued exactly 1 whoami request (got 1)
[proof] expect PASS: scenario1 shutdown prompt: elapsed 200.4ms < 2000ms
[proof] expect PASS: scenario1 persisted nothing (no deviceId, no state files)
[proof] expect PASS: scenario2 control rethrows non-abort retry exhaustion
[proof] expect PASS: scenario2 control made 3 attempts (got 3)
[proof] expect PASS: scenario2 control ran the real backoff schedule (794.8ms)
[proof] expect PASS: scenario2 control error is the transport failure
[proof] expect PASS: no unhandled promise rejections
[proof] RESULT: PASS
EXIT=0
```

Before fix (same script against `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/client/config.ts` from `upstream/main`, restored immediately after): the abort at 200ms is ignored, `whoami` requests #2 and #3 still go out, and the backfill throws at 846.6ms instead of returning promptly.

```text
[proof] config.ts sha256=61df451dc93086ce
[proof] config.ts wires abort into backoff sleep: false
[homeserver] whoami request #1 GET /_matrix/client/v3/account/whoami auth=ok
[proof] scenario1-abort-during-backoff: aborting startup now (200ms mark)
[homeserver] whoami request #2 GET /_matrix/client/v3/account/whoami auth=ok
[homeserver] whoami request #3 GET /_matrix/client/v3/account/whoami auth=ok
[proof] scenario1-abort-during-backoff: outcome=threw error="TypeError: fetch failed"
[proof] scenario1-abort-during-backoff: elapsedMs=846.6
[proof] scenario1-abort-during-backoff: whoamiRequestCount=3
[proof] scenario1-abort-during-backoff: stateDirReadback files=0 deviceIdPersisted=false (state dir untouched)
[proof] expect FAIL: scenario1 resolves undefined after abort
[proof] expect FAIL: scenario1 issued exactly 1 whoami request (got 3)
[proof] RESULT: FAIL (2 unmet expectations)
EXIT=1
```

Regression tests:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/matrix/src/matrix/client.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  23 passed (23)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/index.test.ts
Tests  42 passed (42)
```

`oxlint`/`oxfmt` clean on both changed files; `tsgo` extensions project reports no errors in matrix files.

## Intentionally out of scope

- The other `retryMatrixAuthRequest` call sites (`resolveMatrixAuth` startup whoami, password login) keep their current no-signal behavior; this PR only threads the signal where a real one already exists.
- No change to retry counts, delay bounds, or which errors are retryable.

target.title: fix: gateway boots when a configured plugin payload is broken
target.body:
Refs #109833

PR #110200 has merged into `main`; this branch is rebased onto its merge result.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where gateway readiness was blocked when a configured and enabled plugin package failed startup verification, even though the failure belonged to a known plugin surface that could be isolated.

## Why This Change Was Made

This implements the operator decision on #109833: degrade and boot. Startup quarantines the known plugin owner, emits its typed verification diagnostic once, and skips that plugin before any plugin code can load. Doctor, status, and health expose every quarantined plugin as `configured-unavailable`.

The behavior mirrors degraded SecretRef owners in `src/secrets/runtime-degraded-state.ts` and configured-unavailable channels in `src/channels/status/read-model.ts`. It also follows the root `AGENTS.md` security policy that failures isolate to the smallest known owning surface. The explicit `openclaw update` convergence path remains unchanged and continues to report payload convergence failures prominently.

## User Impact

Operators can keep the gateway ready when one configured plugin package is broken, while the broken plugin remains fully unavailable for that boot and its typed reason stays visible in operational diagnostics. State-migration failures, structurally invalid config, and startup failures with unknown ownership still block readiness.

## Summary

- Records enabled-plugin verification failures as a boot-stable quarantine snapshot refreshed on every Gateway process start.
- Prevents quarantined plugins from reaching artifact resolution or import.
- Keeps package-scoped peer-link inspection failures attached to known plugin ownership; inactive known packages do not block, while genuinely unowned failures remain blockers.
- Projects degraded state through doctor, status, and health, with install paths redacted from public diagnostics.
- Retains the quarantine diagnostic in registry/health state while emitting that exact typed finding only once during startup.

## Root Cause

Before this change, `src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.ts` converted every plugin convergence warning into a fatal startup diagnostic. The design contract in `src/cli/update-cli/post-core-plugin-convergence.ts` explicitly required refusing restart whenever an active installed plugin payload was unloadable, so a known plugin-owned package failure blocked the entire gateway.

Real EACCES proof also exposed two adjacent causes that unit-only proof had missed:

- managed npm peer-link inspection read the same unreadable `package.json` first and converted that known package failure into an ownerless blocking warning;
- the startup migration checkpoint skipped plugin convergence on later processes, so a process-local quarantine could disappear on the second boot while the payload was still broken.

The fix preserves package ownership through peer inspection, refreshes plugin availability on every process start while leaving one-time state migrations checkpointed, and suppresses only the exact loader diagnostic already emitted by startup preflight. PR #110200 supplies the typed package-verification reasons, including unreadable `package.json`; this PR changes only the Gateway readiness policy for known plugin owners.

## Real behavior proof

Built-CLI local process proof on Linux with Node 25.9.0. The fixture is a packed npm plugin with `activation.onStartup: true`; its `register()` writes a sentinel and registers `proof-degrade.ping`. It was installed and enabled through the built CLI in an isolated temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, then its installed `package.json` was changed to mode `000`. A direct same-user Node read returned `EACCES`.

Baseline was built from merge-base/main `03d5d88a14e4`; after proof was built from branch head `9ac87a5d7ba`. Paths below are redacted.

```text
BASELINE (03d5d88a14e4)
gateway_rc=1
readyz_rc=7
plugin_register_marker=absent
[openclaw] Reason: OpenClaw plugin verification failed; refusing to report the gateway ready.
- Failed to repair managed npm OpenClaw host peer links: EACCES: permission denied, open '<PROOF_ROOT>/state/npm/projects/.../package.json'
- Plugin "proof-degrade-plugin" failed post-core payload smoke check (unreadable-package-json): ... EACCES ...
```

```text
THIS BRANCH, broken payload (9ac87a5d7ba)
ready=yes status_rc=0 health_rc=0 doctor_rc=0
plugin_register_marker=absent
typed_startup_diagnostic_count=1
GET /readyz -> {"ready":true,"failing":[]}

status.degradedPlugins = [{
  "pluginId":"proof-degrade-plugin",
  "state":"configured-unavailable",
  "diagnostic":{"kind":"plugin-verification","reason":"unreadable-package-json",
    "detail":"Could not read package.json at <plugin-install>/package.json: EACCES ..."}
}]

health.plugins = {
  "loaded_contains_proof_plugin": false,
  "unavailable": [{"id":"proof-degrade-plugin","state":"configured-unavailable", ...}]
}

doctor:
Plugins configured unavailable
- proof-degrade-plugin (unreadable-package-json): Could not read package.json at <plugin-install>/package.json: EACCES ...
```

```text
SECOND STARTUP, same chmod 000 payload
ready=yes status_rc=0
plugin_register_marker=absent
typed_startup_diagnostic_count=1
GET /readyz -> {"ready":true,"failing":[]}
status.degradedPlugins -> proof-degrade-plugin / configured-unavailable / unreadable-package-json
```

```text
RECOVERY, after chmod 0644 only
ready=yes status_rc=0 health_rc=0 plugin_rpc_rc=0
plugin_register_marker=present
typed_startup_diagnostic_count=0
status.degradedPlugins=[]
health.plugins.loaded_contains_proof_plugin=true
health.plugins.unavailable=[]
gateway call proof-degrade.ping -> {"ok":true}
```

```text
UNCHANGED INVALID-CONFIG BLOCK
gateway_rc=78
readyz_rc=7
Gateway failed to start: Invalid config at <PROOF_ROOT>/invalid-openclaw.json:
gateway.port: Invalid input: expected number, received string
```

All temporary Gateway processes were stopped and the isolated proof state was removed after the PR body update was verified.

## Evidence

Focused quarantine, preflight, peer inspection, doctor, status, health, Gateway, and explicit update-path coverage on the final head:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/commands/doctor-config-preflight.state-migration.test.ts \
  src/cli/update-cli/post-core-plugin-convergence.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor-plugin-registry.test.ts \
  src/plugins/plugin-peer-link.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-startup-plugin-quarantine.test.ts \
  src/gateway/server-plugins.test.ts \
  src/commands/doctor-gateway-health.test.ts \
  src/commands/status.summary.test.ts \
  src/commands/status-overview-rows.test.ts \
  src/cli/update-cli.test.ts

Test Files  10 passed (10)
Tests       366 passed (366)
5 Vitest shards passed
```

## Verification

- `pnpm build` — passed for merge-base baseline and exact final branch head
- `pnpm format <touched paths>` — passed
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed
- `$autoreview --mode uncommitted` — accepted findings were fixed; final passes clean with no actionable findings

## What was not tested

- This was local built-CLI and local Gateway process proof; no container was used.
- No live channel/provider traffic or cross-platform scenario was run. The exercised surfaces were package verification, startup/readiness, plugin import/registration, status, health, doctor, recovery, and invalid-config blocking.

target.title: fix(gmail): prevent duplicate watch renewals during stalls
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Gmail watch renewal could launch duplicate `gog gmail watch start` commands when a previous periodic renewal was still stalled. This affects both the gateway-managed watcher and `openclaw webhooks gmail run` when the configured renewal interval is shorter than the command's two-minute timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each Gmail watcher lifecycle now admits only one periodic renewal at a time. Later timer ticks are coalesced until the active command settles, while existing retry timing, failure logging, configuration, and process lifecycle behavior remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators no longer get overlapping Gmail watch registration commands during slow or stalled renewals. Normal renewals continue on the next interval after the active command settles.

## Evidence

- Focused tests: `src/hooks/gmail-watcher.test.ts` and `src/hooks/gmail-ops.test.ts` — 2 files, 12 tests passed.
- Targeted formatting and lint checks passed for the four changed files.
- Production-lifecycle proof used the real `startGmailWatcher` scheduler and actual child processes. With `renewEveryMinutes: 1`, the first periodic renewal was held for 70 seconds; after 135 seconds exactly two watch-start calls were observed: the initial registration and one renewal. The minute-two tick did not launch a third command.
- An accelerated repeat of the same child-process scenario was captured by the bounded proof runner and produced the same two-call result.
- Fresh open-PR recall found Gmail watcher PRs for delivery mode, OAuth failure handling, secret argv handling, and bind diagnostics, but no PR implementing this single-flight renewal invariant.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users exporting a session to HTML could see a broken replacement glyph in compact tool-call previews when a bash command or serialized tool argument was truncated through an emoji.

The corrupted preview was written into the standalone HTML artifact, so it remained visible when the export was saved or shared.

## Why This Change Was Made

The standalone viewer truncated compact sidebar strings at raw UTF-16 code-unit boundaries. The change uses one surrogate-safe helper for the 50-code-unit assistant bash preview, the 40-code-unit generic argument preview, and the shared sidebar truncation path used by persisted `bashExecution` records. It preserves the existing limits and ellipsis behavior while dropping a boundary surrogate half instead of emitting invalid text.

This is a root-cause, display-layer fix. It does not alter the stored transcript, embedded session data, full tool-call rendering, model input, schema, configuration, or wire format.

## User Impact

Exported HTML transcripts now show stable compact tool labels when long commands or arguments contain emoji at a truncation boundary. Existing ASCII previews and their length limits remain unchanged.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): cancel unread response body on HTTP error + fix(vertex-adc): guard JSON.parse
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #109985

Two fixes:
1. **qa-lab: cancel unread response body on HTTP error** — call `response.body?.cancel()` before throwing on non-2xx responses in `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` so the connection is released back to the pool.
2. **vertex-adc: guard JSON.parse against malformed credential files** — wrap `JSON.parse` in try-catch with a descriptive error message instead of a raw SyntaxError.

## Real behavior proof

### 1. qa-lab response body cancel

**Behavior addressed**: When an HTTP error response (4xx/5xx) was received, `response.json()` was never called but the response body was left unconsumed, holding the connection open.

**Real environment tested**: Node.js test runner (vitest) with mocked `fetch`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```
npx vitest run extensions/qa-lab/web/src/http.evidence.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  7 passed (7)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: Each non-2xx path calls `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)`, covering:
- All error status codes (400, 403, 429, 500, 503) for both `getJson` and `getJsonNoStore`
- Null body (safe: optional chaining `?.`)
- Cancel rejection (suppressed by `.catch(() => undefined)`)

**What was not tested**: `postJson` was not modified — it calls `response.json()` on error to extract an error payload, so body cancel would interfere.

### 2. vertex-adc JSON.parse guard

**Behavior addressed**: Malformed credential files at `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` would cause a raw `SyntaxError` from `JSON.parse`, making debugging harder.

**Real environment tested**: Node.js test runner (vitest) with temp malformed credential file.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```
npx vitest run extensions/google/vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**Observed result after the fix**:
1. The try-catch converts `SyntaxError` → `Error("Google Vertex ADC credentials must be valid JSON: <path>")` (demonstrated via standalone JSON.parse with matching catch logic).

target.title: fix(telegram-miniapp): cancel unread response body on auth error
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the Telegram Mini App page receives a non-ok HTTP response (e.g., 401 auth error), the response body stream is left dangling without being cancelled. This can leak connections and waste resources in the Mini App's WebView environment.

**Root Cause**: The `renderTelegramMiniAppPage()` function's `fetch("auth", ...)` handler was missing `response.body?.cancel()` before `throw new Error("auth failed")`, leaving the response body stream unread and un-cancelled on auth errors.

**Solution**: Add `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the throw, matching the established codebase pattern used across `extensions/chutes/oauth.ts`, `extensions/openrouter/usage.ts`, and other extensions.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Local HTTP server simulating Telegram auth endpoint (401 response), Node.js `fetch` API.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# L2 simulation: auth endpoint returning 401, verify cancel() is called
node docs/.local/issue-109983/verify.mjs
```

**After-fix evidence** (`docs/.local/issue-109983/verify.log`):
```
PASS: response.body.cancel() called on auth error, no unhandled rejection
PASS: response.status = 401 (expected 401)
PASS: response.ok = false (expected false)
PASS: body stream is closed after cancel (done=true)
PASS: repeated cancel() is idempotent
ALL CHECKS PASSED
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 5 checks pass, confirming:
1. `cancel()` is called without unhandled rejection on auth error (401)
2. After `cancel()`, the body stream reports `done=true` (stream properly closed)
3. Repeated `cancel()` calls are idempotent and do not throw

**What was not tested**: Real Telegram WebView environment — the `cancel()` call is browser/WebView API (`ReadableStream.cancel()`), which is simulated here via Node.js `fetch` (which implements the same Web API). The mechanical correctness of inserting `cancel()` before the throw is language-level and does not depend on runtime specifics.

## Tests and validation

All 18 tests across 7 test files pass, including the two page-specific tests and the auth-timeout simulation:

```
 ✓ extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/page.test.ts (2 tests)
 ✓ extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/page.auth-timeout.test.ts (1 test)
 ✓ extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/routes.test.ts (6 tests)
 ✓ extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/command.test.ts (2 tests)
 ✓ extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/init-data.test.ts (2 tests)
 ✓ extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/url.test.ts (3 tests)
 ✓ extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/owner.test.ts (2 tests)

 Test Files  7 passed (7)
      Tests  18 passed (18)
```

- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
